column3: Where is this place?
The fairies call it Puro-Puro. It seems to be the home plane of the implings.
I don't think these creatures have a name for it. As you can see there isn't a lot else here other than wheat.
How did you get here?
The same way you did, I suspect. Through a portal in a wheat field. I followed one back.
I haven't noticed them do that.
That's why I'm the investigator and you're the adventurer.
So, what are these implings?
That's a very interesting question. My best guess is that they are relatives to imps, which is why there are imps here as well.
Implings do appear to like collecting objects and, as my clients have noted, have no concept of ownership. However, I do not sense any malicious intent.
It is my observation that they collect things that other creatures want, rather than they want them themselves. It seems to provide them with sustenance.
So they feed off our desire for things?
Possibly. Either way, it seems that they almost exclusively collect things that people want, except their younglings who I infer haven't learnt the best things to collect yet.
So the more experienced implings have the more desirable items?
That is my observation. Yes.
Can I catch these implings, then?
Indeed you may. In fact I encourage it. You will, however, require some equipment.
Firstly you will need a butterfly net in which to catch them and at least one special impling jar to store an impling.

You will also require some experience as a Hunter since these creatures are elusive. The more immature implings require less experience, but some of the rarer implings are extraordinarily hard to find and catch.

Once you have caught one, you may break the jar open and obtain the object the impling is carrying. Alternatively, you may exchange certain combinations of jars with me. I will return the jars to my clients. In
exchange I will be able to provide you with some equipment that may help you hunt butterflies more effectively.
Also, beware. Those imps walking around the maze do not like the fact that their kindred spirits are being captured and will attempt to steal any full jars you have on you, setting the implings free.
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

Have you indeed? Well, that may well be true, though bear in mind that implings are quite small so they are unlikely to be lugging a sizeable shield around with them. However, since it seems that dragon items are
very desirable to humans then it certainly is possible that the most expert implings may try to obtain such equipment.
So, it's true then? Cool!
I should warn you, though, if the impling is strong enough to collect dragon equipment, then you will have to be very skilled at hunting implings in order to catch them.
Hello. So, what is this place?
This is my home, mundane human! What do you have in your pockets? Something tasty?
Stay out of my pockets! I don't have anything that you want.
Ah, but do you have anything that *you* want?
Of course I do!
Then you have something that implings want.
Eh?
We want things you people want. They are tasty to us! The more you want them, the tastier they are!
So, you collect things that humans want? Interesting... So, what would happen if I caught an impling in a butterfly net?
Don't do that! That would be cruel. But chase us, yes! That is good. Implings are not easy to catch. Especially ones with really tasty food.
So, some of these implings have things that I will really want? Hmm, maybe it would be worth my while trying to catch some.
It's still here.

It's still here. The crop circle is still here.

column3: What's in Puro-Puro?
Implings...and wheat.

Oh, I did notice a very serious-looking gnome go into the portal. Maybe he knows what's going on.
Do you remember what his name was?
Errm, Egg-nog, or something like that.
Right, thanks! I'll have a chat with him when I go. Maybe he'll know what's going on.
So what are these implings then?
Well, no-one knows for sure. The mischievous little creatures are probably related to imps. And they fly as well.
Also, like imps, they love collecting things. I'm not sure why, though. They also seem to like being chased.
So how would I get hold of what they are carrying, then?
Catch them, I suppose. I don't know really. Why would you want to?
Well, if they were carrying something useful. Maybe I could catch them with a big net - like butterflies.
Sounds a bit cruel to me, but I suppose that's possible.
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.
Really? You humans like that stuff a lot, don't you? I don't like really old stuff myself.
Old?
Yes, dragon stuff feels really old.
How can you tell that?
From its magical aura, obviously. Oh, I forget you humans can't feel auras.
How old is old?
Really, really, old.
Can you be any more precise?
Not really. Time doesn't really mean a lot round here. Hundreds, maybe thousands of your human lifespans, I suppose. Anyway, it would have to be old since it all comes from the Necrosyrtes.
Necrosyrtes? Who are they?
Old and powerful creatures. I don't think there have been any around here for aeons. I haven't seen one. I don't think they are very nice. Not like me. Anyway, this is all ancient history. Boooring!
While I'm on the subject do you have any dragon stuff I can have?
Oh, I did have loads, but I threw it away.
What?
Only joking.

No, sorry, I can't help you there. You'll have to look for it yourself. Although, maybe if you find Necrosyrtes then they'll give you some. I heard they give dragon stuff away to people they like. Not fairies. We're too
nice.
No, bye!
See you around!
Is it here? Is it there? Is it elsewhere?
Is what where?
This gate's sister...
I didn't know gates had relations.
Oh yes. This one here - she is calm and boring. She stays here all the time. She doesn't like to move, but her sister is fidgety and refuses to stay in the same place for more than half an hour.
So where is the, errr, fidgety sister at the moment?
Oh well. I don't know what you humans call these places. Let me show you.
Tell me... a story...
Okay...
Perhaps you should empty your hands before you begin.
You tell me a story.
The Third Age of the world was a time of great conflict, of destruction never seen before or since, when all the gods save Guthix warred for control.

The colossal Wyrms, of whom today's dragons are a pale reflection, turned all the sky to fire, while on the ground armies of foot soldiers, goblins and trolls and humans, filled the valleys and plains with blood.

In time the noise of the conflict woke Guthix from His deep slumber, and He rose and stood in the centre of the battlefield so that the splendour of His wrath filled the world, and He called for the conflict to cease!
Silence fell, for the gods knew that none could challenge the power of the mighty Guthix -- for His power is that of nature itself, to which all other things are subject, in the end.
Guthix reclaimed that which had been stolen from Him, and went back underground to return to His sleep and continue to draw the world's power into Himself.
But on His way into the depths of the earth He sat and rested in this cave; and, thinking of the battle-scarred desert that now stretched from one side of His world to the other, He wept.
And so great was His sorrow, and so great was His life- giving power, that the rocks themselves began to weep with Him.
Later, Guthix noticed that the rocks continued to weep, and that their tears were infused with a small part of His power.
So He set me, His servant, to guard the cave, and He entrusted to me the task of judging who was and was not worthy to access the tears.
Not now.

I make leather from animal hides. Bring me some cowhides and one gold coin per hide, and I'll tan them into soft leather for you.
Leather is rather weak stuff.
Normal leather may be quite weak, but it's very cheap - I make it from cowhides for only 1 gp per hide - and it's so easy to craft that anyone can work with it.
Alternatively you could try hard leather. It's not so easy to craft, but I only charge 3 gp per cowhide to prepare it, and it makes much sturdier armour.
I can also tan snake hides and dragonhides, suitable for crafting into the highest quality armour for rangers.
Thanks, I'll bear it in mind.
Hello, and welcome to the Crafting Guild. Accomplished crafters from all over the land come here to use our top notch workshops.

column2: Would you like to ask about a Skillcape of Crafting?

column3: Hey, what is that cape you're wearing? I don't recognise it.
This? This is a Skillcape of Crafting. It is a symbol of my ability as master of the Crafting Guild and it provides unlimited teleports here.
If you should ever achieve level 99 Crafting come and talk to me and we'll see if we can sort you out with one.
Bert! Good news!
Arrr...Good news be always handy.
They arrested Sandy for the murder of a wizard and the sand pit now refills itself!
ME JOB! I'VE LOSTED ME JOB! 'ow c'n yer say tha' be good news?? Me wife'll tear me limb fr'm limb!
Don't worry, the Wizards are going to pay you a large pension so that you can retire...
Bu' wha'll I be doin' wit' me day now! I be lovin' tha sand.
What will you do with your day? Well....You could build sand castles with your own two hands!
I din't think so... bu' iffen yer ever need someone ta haul buckets o'sand 'round, ye be lettin' me know {name}, I's can help yer!
Wow! That would be great, buckets of sand direct to bank everday you say? That's great!
Once per day you may ask Bert to help you by carrying 84 buckets of sand to your bank. Just talk to him!
Rarrg!
What is that cape you're wearing?
This is a Skillcape of Farming, isn't it incredible? It's a symbol of my ability as the finest farmer in the land and wearing it increases my herb yield!
Hello, what are you doing?
Sorry, I don't have time for idle chit-chat, I need to send a fairy to get little Freddies tooth!
Ah don' talk to humans! Yous wanna talk, talk to da boss!
Don' say nuffin' to me! Say it to da boss!
What happened to the old man who used to be the doorman?
You mean my father? He went into retirement, I've taken over the family business instead.
Your father! But you don't look anything like him!
No, fortunately for me I inherited my good looks from my mother.
Who are you?
My name is Zandar Horfyre, and you {name} are trespassing in my tower, not to mention attacking my students! I thank you to leave immediately!

column6: No, I think I'll stay for a bit.

column3: Ok, I was going anyway.
Good! And don't forget to close the door behind you!
No, I think I'll stay for a bit.
Actually, that wasn't an invitation. I've tried being polite, now we'll do it the hard way!
Zamorak curse that mage!
Actually, I guess he already has!
Hello, I've just finished composing my latest poem. Would you like to hear it?
Yes, please.
Excellent! The humans an aficionado! Make yourself comfortable and I'll begin...
Twinkle, twinkle little egg Wouldn't you like to grow some legs? And run around, on grass so green arguing with the milk and cream.
No thanks.
Huh, the cow's right. You humans have absolutely no understanding of art!
What do you want? We're trying to sing! Leave us alone and we won't bother you!
'Ello, sugar. I'm afraid I can't gossip right now, I've got a cake in the oven.
Hello there! Can I sew ye somethin' tegether?

column6: Let me see what you can do.

column3: What do you mean?
Well, ye see it works like this: I can sew yer eye patches onto yer pirate hats or pirate bandanas. Just pirate bandanas mind ye, I hate the feel of snakeskin.
Patchy shudders at the thought of touching snakeskin.
I also sew crab claw gauntlets on to pirate hooks, highwayman masks to black cavaliers, mime masks to black berets, partyhats to glasses and monocles to top hats.
If ye also have some flippers and suitably evil lookin' claws, I can probably put them together too.
It costs 500 coins te do it, and 600 coins te get them separated again afterwards if ye change yer mind.

...I suppose, if that's the kind of person you are.

My pub's called The Legless Faun. It's where all the newcomers find themselves after the long voyage from the east. A good drink takes the edge off, y'know? So, fancy a pint?
Have you heard any rumours here?
Apparently Veos is looking for some help with something. He hangs around the docks of Port Piscarilius.
I'm afraid not as I've something to attend to.
A wise man once told me to never fear a drink... But perhaps I'm a little bias.
'Ello, welcome to my Mining shop, friend!

column3: Can you tell me about pets and pet insurance?
Certainly! You can find pets while out on your adventures. They're very rare, but you may be lucky enough to find one.
You have a chance to find them when defeating bosses, playing minigames, and taking part in skilling activities.
If you do find one, they will be automatically insured against loss, for free!
If you then somehow lose your pet, you can reclaim it here for free also. The service used to cost Reclaim tokens worth 1,000,000 coins each. If you have any of those, I can refund you.
I see, thank you.
I've lost a pet. Have you got it?
If you've lost your pet, it will be reclaimable here!
Let's have a look...
I have a pet that I'd like to insure.
You don't need to pay to insure your pet with me. They're automatically insured for free as soon as you find them!

If you lose a pet somehow, you can come here and reclaim them. It used to cost reclaim tokens, although we're now subsidised by the Grand Exchange and the service is free. If you have any reclaim tokens left, let
us know and we will buy them back.

column3: What pets have I insured?
Every pet you've ever found is automatically insured here!
Here, take a look...
My pet is still lost. Could you look again?
It's possible there was an error in our records. Let me check again for you.
If you believe you have some pets that are not showing on your insurance record, please visit Probita with your pets and she will automatically insure them for you.

column3: I think I'll give the Skullball Course a go.
What are the instructions for using the skullball course?
The skullball comes out of one of these four spawnholes. Just kick the ball through the middle of each goal, through the skeleton's feet.
There are 10 goals, which you must complete in order, and one final goal.
An arrow will point to your ball, just in case lots of people are using the course at the same time as yourself.
The better your time, the more agillity XP you will be awarded. The timer starts when you score your first goal.
How do I use the agility course?
I'll throw you a stick, which you need to fetch as quickly as possible, from the area beyond the pipes.
Be wary of the deathslide - you must hang by your teeth, and if your strength is not up to the job you will fall into a pit of spikes. Also, I would advise not carrying too much extra weight.
Bring the stick back to the werewolf waiting at the end of the death slide to get your agility bonus.
I will throw your stick as soon as you jump onto the first stone.
What is this place?
This is the Skullball Course.
Go and talk to the boss at the beginning of the course if you'd like a go.
Grrr - you don't belong in here, human!
What's beneath the trapdoor?
That's none of your business, human, and I'll never tell.
Oh, come on - I'm only curious.
If it wasn't my duty to stand here and guard our agility course from the likes of you, I would be relieving you of your life right now.
So it's an agility course, then?
No ... yes ... oh blast - you didn't hear me say anything, right?
No problem. Can I come in?
No, human - it's werewolves only.
Who are you? What are you doing here in the snow?
My name is...Sir Gerry. I am...a member of a secret...society of knights. My time is short and I need...your help.
A secret society of knights? What a surprise! Is there an old charter or decree that says if you're a knight you have to belong to a secret order?

I'm sorry, my friend... I do not understand your meaning. Please, time is short... Take this scroll to Sir Tiffy. You will find him in Falador park... You should not...read it... It contains information for his eyes only.
The knight hands you a scroll.
What do you want from me outerlander? It is our policy not to associate with those not of our tribe.

column2: What would you like to ask about?

column3: Where is your chieftain? I find it highly discriminatory to refuse to talk to someone on the grounds that they are not part of your tribe.
I don't rightly understand your speech outerlander, but my loyalty is with Chieftain Brundt.
He resides in our longhall; it is the large building over there, you should speak to him for he speaks for us all.
So what are you doing here?
This should not concern you, outerlander. I am awaiting other Fremenniks to join me on an expedition to Waterbirth Island.
It is a small crescent-shaped island just north-west of here, outerlander.
We have many legends about it, such as the tale of the broken sky, and the day of the green seas.
The reason I am travelling there is more serious Fremennik business, however. I doubt an outerlander would be interested.
Can I come?
An outerlander join us on an honoured hunt???
Well.... I guess... I might be able to allow you to join us, although it is a breach of many of our customs...
Oh, pleeeeease? I really LOVE killing stuff!
Well... I remain unconvinced that it would be wise to allow an outerlander to join us in such dangerous battle, but your enthusiasm seems genuine enough...
I will allow you to escort us, but you must pay me a sum of money first.
What? That's outrageous, why charge me money? And, uh, how much does it cost me?
Ah, the outerlanders have stolen from my people for many years, in this way you can help my community with a small amount of money...
Let us say... 1,000 coins. Payable in advance, of course.
For this I will take you to Waterbirth Island on my boat, and will bring you back here when you have had your fill of the hunt. Assuming you are still alive to wish to leave, of course.
So do you have the 1,000 coins for my service, and are you ready to leave now?
I suggest you head to the cave with some urgency outerlander, the cold air out here might be too much for the likes of you...
No, actually I have some stuff to do here first.
As you wish. Come and see me when your bloodlust needs sating.
Hey, I have to say, that's a fine looking hat you are wearing there.
It is actually a helm, outerlander, but the sentiment is appreciated nonetheless.
Wow, you Fremenniks sure know how to party. Well, see ya around.
Actually, I don't think I have anything to speak to you about...

Well, Ali Morrisane isn't too popular with the other traders in Al Kharid, mainly because he's from Pollnivneach and they feel he has no business trading in their town.

What is there to do round here, boy?
I'm very busy, so listen carefully! I shall say this only once.
Apart from a busy and wonderous market place in Al Kharid to the south, there is the Emir's Arena to the south-east where you can challenge other players to a fight.
If you're here to make money, there is a mine to the south.
Watch out for scorpions though, they'll take a pop at you if you go too near them. To avoid them just follow the western fence as you travel south.
If you're in the mood for a little rest and relaxation, there are a couple of nice fishing spots south of the town.
Thanks for the help!
Hello there!
You seem rather cheerful. Is there anything you're after?

A town to the south of the Shantay Pass, called Pollnivneach.

Not very much, at the moment. I came from further south to set up a smithy here...
...but we still haven't set up the shops, so we have no customers yet.
Hello there!

First you have to weed the patch using a rake.

Not really. I've not done much farming recently.

Sorry. They haven't been delivered yet.

I'm going to set up a shop selling farming implements. That patch out there may be small, but it's all we've got.

Oh, it's a town to the south of the pass, called Pollnivneach.

If I had cloth, patterns and customers, I'd be a tailor. As it is, I'm a tailor with nothing to do.
The silk merchant won't even sell me any silks, because he doesn't trust me!

Pollnivneach. It's a town to the south of the Shantay Pass.

I'm on guard duty. Making sure nobody tries to steal anything from the house and tents in the middle of town.
Why are you only guarding those buildings?
That's all I've been hired to guard.
Hello.
Can't stop sorry! Busy, busy, busy!
Hi.
Greetings. What wisdom do you seek?

column4: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

column3: I'm new to this place. Where am I?

Well young one, you have entered the Magic Training Arena. It was built at the start of the Fifth Age, when runestones were first discovered. It was made because of the many pointless accidents caused by inexperienced
mages.
Who created it?

Good question. It was originally made by the ancestors of the wizards in the Wizards Tower. However, it was destroyed by melee and ranged warriors who took offence at the use of this new 'Magic Art'. Recently,
the current denizens of the Wizards Tower have resurrected the arena including various Guardians you will see as you look around. We are here to help and to ensure things run smoothly.
Interesting. So what can I do here?

You may train up your skill in the magic arts by travelling through one of the portals at the back of this entrance hall. By training up in one of these areas you will be awarded special Pizazz Points unique to
each room. With these points you may claim a variety of items from my fellow guardian up the stairs.
How do you record the points I have earned?
You really are full of questions! You will need a special Pizazz Progress Hat! I can give you one if you so wish to train here.
Yes please!
Ah, I'm afraid I can't give it to you as you don't have room to carry it!
None, I don't really care.
You won't gain with that attitude.
Hi.
Greetings young one. What is it you wish to know?

column4: What do I have to do in this room?
column8: Got any tips that may help me?

column3: What do I have to do in this room?

In this room you will see a maze within which one of my fellow Guardians has been turned to stone for the purposes of this exercise. You must move the statue using your telekinetic grab spell to the exit square at

the edge of the maze to bring the Guardian back to life. Simply stand on the side that you wish for the statue to travel towards and cast the spell on the statue. Once you have solved the maze, the statue will change back

into the Guardian and he will award you with Telekinetic Pizazz Points and teleport you to the next maze. You can switch to a better view of the maze by selecting the 'Observe' option on the statue and return
your view to normal by selecting the same option again. There is also a 'Reset' option on the statue just in case things aren't going too well.
What are the rewards?

As well as the experience in casting magic, you will get Telekinetic Pizazz Points for each maze successfully solved and bonus points for completing five mazes in a row without returning to the entrance.
Got any tips that may help me?

Have a good look at the maze before you try to solve it because this can save you time and runes required to navigate the maze. Although you will still be getting magic experience for moving the statue incorrectly, you
won't be progressing towards collecting Telekinetic Pizazz Points. Lastly, all the mazes can be solved in ten moves or less.
Thanks, bye!
Use what you've learned, young one.
Hi.
Greetings young one. What wisdom do you seek?

column8: Got any tips that may help me?

column3: What do I have to do in this room?

In this room you will see various cupboards. It is your task to search the cupboards to find items to turn into gold using your low or high alchemy spells. You can deposit the money in the receptacle at the end of the

hall in order to receive your Alchemist Pizazz Points. This money is used for the upkeep of the training arena as well as magic shops all around Gielinor. Keep an eye on the costs of each item as these will change
from time-to-time, as will the location of the items. Occasionally one of the items will be indicated as costing no runestones to convert to money.
How will I be rewarded?

You will get magic experience from casting the alchemist spells, as well as 1 Alchemist Pizazz Point for every 100 coins you deposit, and 10% of the coins you deposit will be given to you as you leave. Keep in mind that you
will not be able to take more than 1000 coins back out with you.
Got any tips that may help me?

You must remember to keep an eye on the various costs of the items. If you watch the movements of the other players, you might be able to guess which are the best places to visit. You will get 1 Pizazz Point for
every 100 coins, so if you have 190 coins, why not get an extra 10?
I see.

Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave this room by a method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed, but the gold
coins and Pizazz points you earned will be granted.
Thanks, bye!
Use what you've learned, young one.
Hello.
Greetings young one. How can I enlighten you?

column3: What do I have to do in this room?

In this chamber you will see various piles of shapes. You can pick up these shapes and enchant them using the enchant jewelry spells. By enchanting these shapes, you'll be converting them into orbs which you can be

placed in the hole in the centre. You will get Enchantment Pizazz Points for every ten shapes that you convert and the points you get depends on the level of enchantment spell you cast. You will get a
bonus Pizazz Point for enchanting a certain shape at a certain time, which I will periodically shout out. You will also be rewarded with an item for every so many orbs you deposit into the hole.
What are the rewards?

As well as the magic experience from casting your enchantment spells, you will get Enchantment Pizazz Points for converting so many shapes, plus a bonus point for converting a shape of the correct type. You
should also note that you will occasionally be rewarded with items when you put one of the enchanted orbs in the floor.
Got any tips that may help me?

Try to guess or keep track of the time between the changes of the best shape to enchant. This means you can be ready to run to a different shape when you know it is about to change. Look out for the dragon
gems, as these will get you more Pizazz Points!
I see.

Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave this room by a method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.
Thanks, bye!

column3: What do I have to do in this room?

Have you noticed all the bones around the room? These are teleported here from all over Gielinor to help clean up the landscape of countless bones left behind from combat. What better use for these bones than to

convert them to nutritious fruit to be eaten by you mortals? You have to use your Bones to Bananas spell to convert the bones and then place them in the holes on the walls to earn Graveyard Pizazz Points.
Unluckily for you, your health will constantly decrease from getting hit by these dropping bones so you will probably want to eat some of the bananas yourself to increase your stay here.
What are the rewards?

You will get experience from casting your bones to bananas spell and you will get Graveyard Pizazz Points when you put the bananas through the wall. Occasionally you will also be credited with a runestone
to help you in your future spell casting.
Got any tips that may help me?

Different bones will provide you with different numbers of bananas, so try to find the best type. Collect enough points and you will be able to buy a 'Bones to Peaches' spell from my fellow guardian above the entrance hall.
This spell can be used here just like the bones to bananas spell, except this spell will give you even more experience and the peaches will restore more health!
I see.

Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave this room by a method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.
Thanks, bye!

I'll keep track of the work you do as well and give you some points for our company reward shop.
Also there are assistants in Varrock, Ardougne, and Hosidius that can give you work, if Falador is inconvienent for you.
The clients that I would offer you to go help could be in any of those cities, it might be a bit of a journey to get there!

column3: Tell me about this village.
You want to know about Canifis? I dunno why, not a lot happens here. We're just your typical everyday down at earth werewolf folk, after all...
So... everyone here is a werewolf?
Yep. We are as Zamorak made us!
You mentioned Zamorak...
Yeah, he's great isn't he? Every year we hold a big festival to give thanks to Zamorak for keeping us well fed and happy here.
I hear over in the West they worship Saradomin, but I dunno why! What's he ever done to help out us werewolves, huh?
I hear he has all these crazy followers who say things like we shouldn't kill people and eat them! What's up with that?
...So when is this festival?
Aaaah, not for a good few months yet. Come and ask me again nearer to the time, I'll keep some extra meat and mead back from the rest for ya pal.
Tell me about the land of Morytania.

Well, I don't know what to tell you really... This village is called Canifis and lies on the border between Morytania and Misthalin... so we're kind of on the front line if those Saradominists to the west ever decide to
attack us...
That doesn't seem likely...
No? The Saradominists hate us. It's only thanks to Lord Drakan that these lands are kept safe.
Lord Drakan? Who is that?
Ahhh... you must be new to these parts if you haven't heard of Lord Drakan! He's the lord of this land, and we all pledge allegiance to him.
In return for our allegiance, and the tithe of course, he keeps our land safe from any invaders and the Saradominists who want to kill us all.
Tithe? What do you mean?

Ah, well, in return for his protection, we have to give Lord Drakan a share of blood every week. If we don't have any to spare from our hunts, then we need to pick a member of the village to give their life in return
for the blood so that the tithe is fulfilled.
You mean you kill someone you know in order to meet the tithe???

That's right, but only if we haven't managed to get enough spare blood from our hunts. It's kind of severe if you look at it that way, but frankly, I think the price is fair in return for his protection and his tolerance of
our village. He could probably kill us all if he wanted us gone, so keeping on his good side is worth the sacrifice to us. Lucky we're not human really!
Why's that?
He hates humans! Apparently his brother Draynor is trapped in Misthalin, and adventurous little human wannabe-heroes keep trying to kill him!
Tell me about the shopkeepers here.
Hmmm? Why, who did you want to hear the gossip about?
Tell me what you know about Sbott the Tanner.

Hey, I won't hear a word said bad about that guy! He's an honest and hard-working wolf if I ever met one! He charges a lot for his job, but he's one of the best tanners I've ever seen - and I'm over four hundred
years old! You need stuff tanning, I recommend him!
Know anything interesting about Rufus the food seller?

Ah yeah... good old Rufus... He's kind of getting on in years and doesn't like to come out of his wolf form so often, but let me tell you this: that guy is a hunter through and through. You seen how much food he

catches a day? That takes real dedication! Some of the young pups think just because a wolf has a bit of grey in his fur then he's past it, but I've seen him put those pups to shame in a hunt! He's a real inspiration to us
all!
Got anything to share about Barker the clothes seller?
Eh, I don't like the guy much, but you can't knock the quality of his stock. They're some fine quality threads you can get yourself there.
What's wrong with him?
Eh... I can't really tell you to be honest. Something about the guy just gets my hackles up everytime he opens his yap, know what I mean?
No, not really.
Lucky for you. I can't really explain it, I just don't like the guy. Does great clothes though, you got to give him that.
I bet you have some juicy gossip about Fidelio the general store owner.

That nut job? Oh sure, we all know about him. He was a real firebrand daredevil when he was younger, always taking risks to make himself a quick buck... he got himself caught up in the smuggling trade, sneaking over
the border into Misthalin and pretending to be a human so he could buy exotic items to sell.
Exotic items? From Misthalin? Like what?
Oh man, you name it! Flour... buckets... tinderboxes... chisels... he could get the lot! He's been doing it so long now though, his nerves are shot.
Nowadays he's a disgrace, he can barely string a sentence together and jumps at his own shadow. Makes you feel ashamed to be a werewolf.
Tell me about the temple to the west.
Well, I'm not old enough to remember the full story behind it, but it was a terrible day for these lands when it was built there.
Apparently, Morytania was once a strong and mighty kingdom, with lands spreading far further west than they do today, and south into the desert as well.

That was all until the day when a sneak attack by the hated human forces who worship Saradomin burned our villages and slaughtered our peoples in mass. To rub salt into the wound, they then cursed the river as well!
Luckily they seem to have calmed down somewhat recently, and tend to stay on their side of the river... but the wrong they have done my people will never be forgotten, and will never be forgiven!
So you hate humans?
Absolutely! If I ever met one I would gobble him up where he stands! And then chew the bones for dessert!
Um, okay, thanks, bye.
Can I hear a story?
A story??? Heh, well the only one I can think of right now is one my dear old mammy told me as a pup...
Now how did it go... Ah yes!

Once upon a time a brave young wolf was walking through a forest, when he came upon a human dressed all in red. 'Aha!' he thought to himself, 'Here's a nice easy meal!' But the human talked to him, and as he was
always taught to be a polite wolf, he spoke back to it.

Well, this cunning human told him that there was a better meal that would not run away in a house in the woods. As the brave young wolf could see that this human was not fully grown, he figured maybe he'd

better get a better meal at this house, so he ran as fast as his paws could carry him to the house the human told him about... inside he found an old human lying in bed, and although the meat was a little tough, as the

human was older than he thought, he had a good meal and decided to sleep it off in the house for awhile. He had not been asleep long though, when he was woken by a knocking at the door. The human in red had followed

him to the house! Suspecting a human trap, the brave young wolf put on the old humans clothes and jumped into the bed, so that he could pretend to be human and escape from this terrible trap! Well now, this human

dressed in red came into the house, and pretended to believe the brave wolf was really a human, and began to talk to him. But then the human started asking strange questions of the wolf, because the human knew that it

was not a human at all! The brave young wolf decided to try and escape, for it was only a young human, and not very strong, so the brave young wolf said he would eat the human if they did not let him escape! As he said

this however, the human in red shouted out at him: 'Aha! You are a wolf!' and as the human shouted this another bigger human ran into the room from outside! This bigger human was much stronger and was
carrying an axe, and the poor young wolf died in this terrible trap made for him by the humans.
And do you know what the moral of this story is?
Um... no, not really.
It's 'Never trust humans' of course! My dear old mammy told me that story when I was a pup, and I'm still alive and well to tell it to you today!
Pretty good story huh?
Um... yeah. It was great. Really.
Nothing thanks.
...I don't know why you talked to me if you don't want anything then...

Prospector Percy discovered unusual mineral veins in this cave. Now he's built a machine to let us extract useful ores.
Percy calls it the Motherlode. I don't know why, and I'm not asking - that's between him and his mother.
Dwarves don't normally let humans claim areas of the mine like this, but Percy's machine is really useful, so we struck a deal.

I'm happy here... the voices tell me I'm happy here. I can continue my work.

I built this chapel here so that fighters could come and pray before battle. A fighter who ignores their spiritual needs may as well have stabbed themselves in the foot.
People keep claiming they're not interested in religion, but as soon as they're under attack they're yelling for 'Protect from Melee'. Sad, really.
So is there something I can do for you?
So whose sister are you?
Ahahahahahaha, very funny! With jokes like that, you should become a banker.
But no I am a sister to the broken and down trodden, I heard talk of this enclave being built and knew that my skills could be put to good use.
I've found a worthy cause here running my little chapel, so I'm happy enough. Now, can I help you with something?
I'm fine, thanks.

I collect valuable resources and pawn off access to them to foolish adventurers, like yourself.
You should take a look inside my arena. There's an abundance of valuable resources inside.

Not right now.

Not right now.
Hello.
Greetings.
Who are you?
I am an architect. I designed and built many of the buildings in Arceuus using magic.
How exciting!
It is an honour to serve my city in such a way. Now, I am very busy, please leave.
Hey there, what can I do for ya?
My name is Drew and I man this here grinding machine. I call her Sandstorm!
I can also look after any buckets ya want me to.
Me and Sandstorm go way back, we started off back in the desert mining camp, I was a slave and I had the honour of looking after Sandstorm.
How did you and Sandstorm get out of the mining camp?
Well, because I was in charge of looking after Sandstorm, I was able to look at the inner workings.

While the guards weren't looking, I would take apart Sandstorm piece by piece and place the pieces in boxes and barrels, when Sandstorms inners were all gutted, I tricked the cart driver by telling him cart jokes.
So, he didn't bother to check his cargo and I was able to board as he was driving off.
Anyway, that's all in the past. Can I help ya with anything else?
You haven't got any buckets for me to hold.
Ya don't have any buckets of sand to withdraw. Ya need to give me empty buckets, and grind sandstone in my grinder, then I'll sell ya buckets of sand.
Nothing sorry. I have to be going now.
Oh, bye then.
Hello again. How are you?
What's that? How do I chew? With my teeth of course. You humans are odd.
No, no I said HOW ARE YOU?
No need to shout, I'm not deaf. I'm good thank you.
Dooooom!
Where?
All around us! I can feel it in the air, hear it on the wind, smell it... also in the air!
Is there anything we can do about this doom?
There is nothing you need to do my friend, for I am the Doomsayer! I roam the world sensing danger.
If I find a dangerous area, then I put up warning signs that will tell you what is so dangerous about that area.

column6: Thanks, I'll remember that if I see any warning signs.

How do I farm here?
Let's see... First, you'll need to treat the soil with saltpetre. Dig it into the patch with a trowel. The minerals are good for the fruit.
Then plant a grape seed, and just let it grow. I'll look after it, so it won't get diseased.
When your grapes are ready, pick them and clear the patch so you can grow a new vine.
Does that seem clear, or would you like help with something else?
What do you do?
I'm the vintner. I helped Lord Hosidius to develop this land as a vinery, and now it's complete he's put me in charge of production while he works on a new project.
His son, young Pandur, works here too. Pandur checks the wine I produce. But if you've got any questions about the farming, don't ask Pandur. Ask me instead. He checks the wine too much.
Why are you called Gallow?
It's short for 'Gallows'. When I was young, a boy made some improper suggestions to me, so I grabbed him by his neck and held him in the air until he learnt some manners.
Now, dear, do you need help with the vinery? I'm enjoying the chat, but I have work to do.
I'm fine, thanks.
Hello.
Excuse me!

Can't you see I'm on the toilet?

Yeah. A toilet.
Riiiight. Oh, man, you didn't wipe your hands?
Get over it.
Hello.
Are you an architect?
Oh hello there, you've come to the right place.
I wondered if you might have some time to help...?
I am sorry but the people of Port Piscarilius does not favour you currently. I have to get back to my duties.
Greetings!
Oh hello there, I'm an architect.
I wondered if you might have some time to help...?
So sorry, too busy at the moment.
That statue is truly awesome!
Isn't it just!
After years of planning, the humans are going to get what they deserve.
You! Get out of my way!
Welcome to my private little wyvern area.

column8: So are you a Slayer Master?

column3: Who are you?
I'm Steve. You may have heard of my big cousin Nieve - she's one of the Slayer Masters. She's the famous one in the family. But Nieve's not here - this area's mine
Why is this wyvern area private?
Because I say so! My cousin Nieve thinks she's so great because she's got a big cave where she can boss people around. So I carved some steps out of the ice, and made myself a training area here.
So are you a Slayer Master?
No, I'm not. My cousin Nieve is a Slayer Master. There's nothing special about her, you know. All she does is tell people to kill stuff. That's Slayer Masters for you.
Thanks, goodbye.
Welcome to my private little wyvern area.

column6: Why is this wyvern area private?
column8: So are you a Slayer Master?

column3: Who are you?
I'm Pieve. My big brother Steve made this training area, but he's gone off to be a Slayer Master to replace our cousin Nieve, so this area's mine now.
Why is this wyvern area private?
My brother, Steve, carved the steps to get up here. He was jealous of our cousin, Nieve, because she'd got a huge training cave where she could boss people around. So he made this place.
So are you a Slayer Master?
No, I'm not. My brother Steve is a Slayer Master. He took over the job from our cousin Nieve. All he has to do is tell people to kill stuff - he says it's easy!
Thanks, goodbye.
Got a medpack? I feel terrible.
What happened to you?
Lizardman bite. There's always a fever after you've been bitten by one of those. I'm sure they don't clean their teeth.
Sorry, I haven't got one.
Try looking in the storage tents outside.
What do you want?
What are you guarding?
This path leads to the Doors of Dinh. You should be careful if you wish to travel any further.

column4: Tell me about the Doors of Dinh.

column3: Tell me about the Doors of Dinh.
They're to keep the Wintertodt at bay. No-one knows what it really is, but centuries ago it came out of the northern wastes to terrorise the kingdom.
The Doors were created by Dinh, a master smither, to imprison the Wintertodt.
Now we keep a watch on the pass, so that the armies can be summoned if the Wintertodt ever escapes.
Okay, thanks for the warning.
Okay, thanks for the warning.
Who are you?
I'm the duty look-out on the northern pass. It's the worst assignment there is.
As if the cold weren't bad enough, the snooty Arceuus magi always look down their noses at the Shayzien armies, just because we use muscle and steel rather than fancy magicks.
I'll leave you alone now.
As you can see, we are busy. What do you want?

column4: What is all this paper for?

column3: What is all this paper for?
This paper, as you call it, contains strategies for use in the war against the lizardmen. The details are a military secret, so do not ask any more questions.
Fair enough.
I don't want anything.
Then be off with you!
Please do not disturb our deliberations.
What are you deliberating?
Lord Shayzien wishes us to draw up contingency plans for various scenarios in the ongoing war against the lizardmen.
If they ever succeed in cutting us off from Lovakengj, our supply lines will be severely constrained, and I must work on alternative plans.
So please do not disturb us further.
I'll leave you to it.
Oh, sorry.

I used to work down at the beach, running the charcoal furnaces, but I've handed all that business to my son now. He's a good boy.
Anyway, retiring isn't too bad. There's plenty of warmth from the lava pits, and my boy helps me carry my shopping from Munty's shop. I'll be alright.
But you've never told me what you're doing in my house, young man. Don't think I've forgotten!
Have you got anything to trade?
Oh, are you a door-to-door salesman? My boy said I shouldn't let people like you into the house, and to call the guards if you bothered me.

Thanks!
Welcome to the woodcutting guild. How may I help you?
Tell me about the guild.

I founded the woodcutting guild when I retired from the Shayzien military. I spotted the ancient redwood trees in the hills many years ago from the Shayzien camp, and decided to construct the guild around them.
You can find them to the West, just follow the path.

However, if you're skilled in combat, or simply afraid of heights, the ent cavern may be more suited for you. The ents dwell deep beneath the ancient redwoods, and can be accessed through the cave to the North-West.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
That's all, thanks.
Tell me about yourself.
My name is Lars, and I am the founder of the woodcutting guild. I originally grew up in a Shayzien camp, and was raised on the battlefield.
As I grew older, I found peace in Hosidius, and the joys of skilled labour. I turned in my battleaxe for a hatchet, and set up a guild for those also talented in the skill of woodcutting.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
That's all, thanks.
I'm just passing by.
Sure, let me know if there's anything I can do for you.
Hello.
Hello, how can I help you?
What's in this cave?
Creatures known as ents inhabit the depths of the hills, rumour has it they reside there due to the presence of the ancient redwood trees on the hills.
If you're as skilled a fighter as you are a woodcutter, you may enter the caves. You should find Kai once you are inside, he can give you some more information.
I was just passing through.
Hello! Who are you?
Hi there, my name is Kai and I'm the keeper of this here ent habitat.
What exactly is an ent?
Good question! Ents are ancient beings that resemble trees, we believe they draw their energy directly from nature.
Where did they come from?
Another good question! We're not sure exactly, we just know they're a very old race.
I have heard of similar creatures roaming a desolate part of the eastern continent, though.

Oh most certainly! I write about all the objects in the lands. From weapons and armour to palm trees and sands. That's why I wander far from Rellekka to seek inspiration.
I have one problem though. I am very forgetful, I can never remember which particular object a song was about.
Surely the lyrics for such a song would be enough to help you remember?
I am afraid not. It saddens me deeply, so I often send out messages to adventurers to help me discreetly.

DO NOT defy him! Give him your eggs! So colourful! So beautiful!
I'm going to leave you alone now.

What sort of things do you crush?
All kinds of things! Unicorn horns, goat horns, blue dragon scales and much more besides. Hand me your stuff, and I'll try to crush it. I charge 50 coins per item.
Who are you?
I'm Wesley. I used to work on a big ship, exploring the world with my mother, but then I didn't get on very well at the fleet's training school, so I quit all that.
So I moved to Nardah and took up this job crushing stuff instead. It's always been a passion of mine, crushing things. I'm a lot happier now.
The world is so much simpler when you're crushing. You know you just have to grind for long enough until you get the job done. It might take hours, but you just grind until you're done.
I'm not interested, thanks.
That's no use!
Welcome back, brother. How may I be of assistance?
Are you here to fight the cold?
Umm... I guess?
Great! Ask me anything you like about the Bruma tree, I'm an expert.

column6: Tell me about the Bruma tree.

column3: Tell me about the Wintertodt.
Some would say that ice preserves while fire destroys, but no amount of fire is destroying the Wintertodt. That's a cold that will freeze the air in your lungs.
Even the heat generated from burning the Bruma roots only weakens it, and that doesn't last very long nowadays.
Looks like an angry snow storm to me...
What you see in that pit is not the Wintertodt at full strength. It never will be while the Bruma tree still burns and the Doors of Dinh remain closed.
Tell me about the Bruma tree.
The Bruma tree is what keeps the Wintertodt weak. The prison was built here by Dinh because of its usefulness against the Wintertodt.
Some legends say that Xeric is the cause for the Doors weakening, or maybe he made the Wintertodt stronger?
Is Xeric really such a bad guy?
It's a known fact that he was interested in the Bruma tree. For what purpose... there are only rumours.
Regardless, the Bruma tree definitely contains powerful magic. I've been studying the sap for years and it has truly astounding properties.
There's not many fires that burn green now, are there?
What about gnomish fire lighters?
Tell me about yourself.
Me? I'm a member of the Woodcutting Guild. More of a researcher though... I'm currently tasked with growing a new Bruma tree.
How's that going?
Poorly. I believe the Bruma tree can only be grown in a freezing cold climate.
Well, isn't that here?
It's just an idea really. For all I know, it could be magic way beyond me, beyond even the Pyromancers.
See you later.
Goodbye!
Hello there.
Tell me about the Wintertodt.
Ignisia claims it's some kind of evil spirit.
You don't believe her?
Nah, I believe in things I can stab and kill. This is all just a storm in a teacup. I mean, how can wind and snow be evil? My toad is more of a threat!
Your... toad?
Yeah, just a bit of fun. I have a pet - he's around here somewhere, assuming that troublesome cat hasn't eaten him.
That's a bit weird, but okay.
No weirder than being scared of snow.
Tell me about yourself.
I'm Captain Kalt, proud member of the Shayzien Army.
How long have you been a soldier?
Man and boy I've worn the uniform. Earned Captain a few years back and never looked back. Not too happy about babysitting delusional wizards though. But orders is orders.
Tell me how I'm doing.
Go play in the snow and come back when you've done something.
See you later.
Goodbye.
Be on your guard friend.

column8: What do you think of the Pyromancers?

column3: Tell me about the Wintertodt.
The Wintertodt terrorised Great Kourend many centuries ago. It destroyed much of this northern land over many years before it was finally driven back into this prison.
Why did it attack Kourend?
No one knows for sure but I have a theory...
Which is?
The Dark Altar. It felt the altar's power and wanted to consume it for itself. It wouldn't be the first time...
Interesting...
Tell me about yourself.
I'm Ish, one of the navigators of Piscarilius.
What brings a navigator up here?
Lady Piscarilius has sent me here to keep an eye on the situation. She doesn't trust the other houses and believes something sinister is going on.
Like what?
I don't know, but I intend to find out.
What do you think of the Pyromancers?
I've heard stories about them and the things they have done over the years. Be careful, they can't be trusted.
You seem a bit paranoid.
Better to be paranoid than a fool. Anyone with any sense knows that the Pyromancers are trouble. They say even Lord Arceuus doesn't trust them.
I have to go.
Stay vigilant friend.

I used to stalk the night drinking blood like vampyres do, and I am certainly not just a role-playing enthusiast in a costume! Never question that!

Granddad's fruit farm. It's a right dump. This whole corner of the city is a dump.

column4: So why are you here if it's a dump?

column3: So why are you here if it's a dump?
My cow of a sister kicked me out of her bar. Said I was getting the place a bad name. So I'm staying here until I'm old enough to get my own place.
I want to move to Arceuus. It's properly awesome up there. I'll do bartending or something until I can learn to be a necromancer.
Anyway, why are you here? Do you want something?
Never mind.
Okay, thanks for the info.
Yeah, you're in the biggest dumpster of Dumpsterville. Now you know. Anyway, do you want something?
Tell me about yourself.
Yeah, alright...
I am Bologa Gricoller, seeker of forbidden wisdom, wanderer of the dark pathways, thinker of the unthinkable. I can do bartending too.
I used to work at The Golden Field. That's my sister's bar. It's mostly farmhands drinking there, but you get some interesting people as well.
See, most Hosidius people are Saradominists. My sister, she's always listening to Father Jean at the church with his goodie-goodie sermons.
But some of us in the bar thought we'd give Zamorak a try. Like, you gotta be open-minded, right? What did Saradomin ever do for us anyway?
So we'd meet in the bar, sharing books that the Piscarilius smugglers would bring us, learning what the Saradominists don't want us to know.
Anyway, my sister - she's a right cow, by the way - she fired me and kicked me out. Said I was bringing bad sorts to her bar.
Bad sorts, she said! Like, morality is totally subjective, right? So who's she to call us bad sorts just 'cos we're not afraid to think differently?
Anyway, I've learnt all this cool stuff about Zamorak, and being stuck in a fruit farm doesn't stop me being his loyal servant, right?
In fact I've invented a Zamorakian blessing that works on fruit! You can use it to make Zamorak's wine out of grapes from the Vinery.

column4: Can you help me to make Zamorak's wine?

column3: Can you help me to make Zamorak's wine?

How'd that work out for them?
Pretty well - only one died. Still, they got it working...sort of. This ancient technology can be tricky.
What do you mean, 'sort of'? Altars either work or don't work.
This one works, just not as you'd expect. You put pure essence in, but get random runes back. Some of them we don't even know how to craft!
Sounds like a pretty good deal. Can I give it a go?

I don't think so. The mages don't like outsiders going in; they'll probably attack you. They only patrol the short path, though, so if you used the long path, through a tunnel near the entrance, you'd probably be safe.

I can see it all ending badly, but that's the problem with intellectuals - they always think they know better.
Anyway, maybe they'll all get themselves killed. Then we can put the barricade back up.
If you go out there yourself, give the lizardmen a kicking from me. They've killed too many of my soldiers.
Good day to you bwana.

Uh huh, that's a mighty fine gold necklace you have.
Well bwana, of course I take a cut, but the funds keep these beaches clean and tidy, I promise!

Good day to you too.

Made from the wood of the Fyburglars tree, strong and light weight! Perhaps if it went missing, I'd find you.
Perhaps.
Hello there.

From boatman to researcher? That's quite the change.

If that isn't exciting, I don't know what is.

Goodbye for now.

Is it?
Well, he told me it was his last one too, so I figured I'd give it a try.
It was nice meeting you William.
I bet!

column3: Horologist? What does that mean?
Horology is the study and measurement of time. Specifically, I study how time and dates have been historically recorded.
For example, the date convention in Great Kourend is to state the number of days and decades since the signing of the Royal Accord of Twill.

column3: Tell me more about the Royal Accord of Twill.
The Royal Accord of Twill was signed by the rulers of each of the houses 139 decades ago, following the great famine.
The Accord declared that each house will, in turn, rule the Kingdom of Great Kourend for one decade in rotation, based on lots drawn.
You may find a book in the Grand Library with further information. Is there anything else I can help you with?

column4: Is the Royal Accord of Twill still honoured today?

column3: Is the Royal Accord of Twill honoured today?
Our kingdom has advanced somewhat over the many decades since the Accord. Though some parts of the Accord remain intact, the Kourend Council now rules Great Kourend.
Was the Accord ever breached?
Indeed it was. In the 13th decade, King Shayzien III seized control of Kourend using the military under his command.
The full set of laws within the Accord haven't been followed since. However, some of them were reinstated in the 47th decade, by King Byrne I.
Fascinating. What happened during that time?
During the 20th decade, King Shayzien VI married the daughter of Lord Hosidius. Four decades later their son was crowned king.
He took the name King Hosidius IV in an attempt to distance the family from the breaking of the Royal Accord of Twill.
King Hosidius IV followed by his son, King Hosidius V ruled Kourend until the early days of the 33rd decade.
It was then that King Shayzien VII took control of the kingdom. His rule was a notably violent one.
King Shayzien VII was killed some five decades later during the Battle of the Concourse. He was succeeded by the dark mage, Xeric.
Xeric ruled Kourend for more than ten dark decades using an army of lizardmen. This time period was known as the Age of Strife.
Xeric was eventually killed during the 47th decade and succeeded by King Byrne I.

The Tower was constructed by King Rada III. We don't know exactly when, since dates were not recorded before the Twill Accord.

More than 137 decades ago, seemingly from nowhere, the Wintertodt began terrorising the lands north of Kourend, freezing everything within its path.
After five decades of this terror, the people of Kourend were able to quell the beast, containing it in an icy prison.
The Wintertodt remained subdued until very recently, when it began to threaten Kourend once more.
Fortunately, the Order of the Sacred Flame is able to contain the Wintertodt and prevent another attack.

column3: Who was Xeric?
Xeric was a dark mage who ruled Great Kourend for at least ten decades. A time period that is sometimes known as the Age of Strife.
At least? Do you not know how long he was in power for?
We do have records of course. However, while Xeric was indeed ruler of the kingdom from the 37th to the 47th decades, some believe that he actually ruled for longer.
How come?
It is often speculated that Xeric and his predecessor, King Shayzien VII, were in fact the same person.
How could that be?
Like Xeric, King Shayzien VII was fascinated with the Dark Altar.
The King was killed at the Battle of the Concourse during the 37th decade. We have many accounts of this, yet his body was never recovered.
Just days after his death, we have the first recorded mention of Xeric, an incredibly powerful mage who resembled the King.
It is written that Xeric killed the rulers of Kourend's five cities and claimed the kingdom as his own.
So King Shayzien VII was resurrected as Xeric using the Dark Altar?
It's possible. I am no expert on necromancy but we know the Dark Altar has the power to resurrect beasts. We also know that it can extend life. It's how the people of Arceuus are immortal.
King Shayzien VII may have found a way to combine these powers.
How did Xeric have so much power?
Xeric drew much of his power from the Dark Altar, but he asserted his authority as ruler through his personal army of creatures, the lizardmen.
Xeric created the lizardmen!?
Sadly so, though we're not exactly sure how he did so. Xeric used the citizens of Kourend for many experiments, as well as for his own sadistic pleasures.
We have little written record of the experiments, but we believe they might have led to the creation of the lizardmen.
Do you know why he created the lizardmen?
Xeric was undoubtedly powerful, but he couldn't rule the people singlehandedly, nor could he rely on human informants. He needed an army he could control.
Lizardmen are loyal creatures and would do as he commanded without question. With them at his disposal, the people were powerless to resist his authority.

column3: What happened to the lizardmen after Xeric's reign?
They remain loyal to Xeric. Even to this day they continue to attack the kingdom, as you may have seen.
Fortunately, the Shayzien Army keeps them under control.
Why do they keep fighting? Surely after a thousand years they must know Xeric is gone?
Without examining their minds, we will never know for sure. However, we assume Xeric genetically altered them to enforce that their duty is to serve him.
But if they are serving Xeric, why do they attack the kingdom?
A good question. One that I'm afraid I do not know the answer to.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
What happened to Xeric?
During the 47th decade, after ten decades of oppression, the people revolted against Xeric and his army of lizardmen.
Why did the people suffer for so long?
The events were triggered through the courage of one man, Byrne. He was not a man of particular stature of nobility, though he did proceed to become king.
What happened?
'Twas the 312th day of decade 47. Byrne, a farmer by trade, is said to have witnessed a lizardman guard murder a child whilst working his farm.
Outraged at what he had just seen, Byrne grabbed his pitchfork and sprinted towards the guard.
Blinded by fury, Byrne attacked the guard, slaughtering the lizardman in plain sight of all around.
Legend has it Byrne then gave a galvanizing speech, standing over the butchered guard with his bloodied pitchfork held aloft in the air, urging the people to fight back.
Do you know what he said?
Sadly no. While we have many witness accounts, they all differ, so we can not verify it at all.
Ah, so what happened next?
Whatever Byrne said, the people responded. Together, the citizens of Kourend revolted, grabbing whatever they could use as a weapon. They fought the lizardmen.
The lizardmen, while strong and powerful, were simply outnumbered. In a matter of days, they had been driven back into the Kebos Lowlands.
So what happened to Xeric?
During the battle, the temple surrounding the Dark Altar was destroyed, weakening Xeric's power. We believe he fled to Quidamortem.
Some say Xeric was actually killed during the revolt, but we have no record of his remains being discovered.
So no one knows what really happened to him?
Xeric was incredibly powerful but we can reasonably assume that he soon perished. Without the power of the Dark Altar, Xeric would have become mortal.

You should speak to the Curator as he knows more about it than I.

column3: What is Deadman mode?
Deadman mode is an incredibly dangerous survival game mode. Anyone can attack anyone, anywhere. Death comes at a huge cost and killing other players can be extremely lucrative.
Lucrative, you say?

Killing a player will earn you all of the items they had on them, plus the 10 most valuable items from their bank. The unfortunate soul will also lose half of their experience in most skills, or a quarter if they were not skulled. Regardless, it's quite the set-back.
Wow, that is brutal!
It is, but it is no simple task to kill someone in Deadman mode.
Very high level guards patrol every major city and bank. They will kill anyone who has a skull. Getting yourself a kill is only half the battle.
How do I play Deadman mode?
You can log into Deadman mode by selecting a Deadman mode world from the world list before you log in.
So I don't need a new account to play Deadman mode?
Nope! You can use your existing account on a Deadman world, providing you have membership.
Do my stats and items transfer over to Deadman mode?
No, they do not. Your Deadman mode progress is completely separate from normal Old School worlds.
What happens when I die in Deadman mode?
If you die to a player you will lose the 10 most valuable stacks of items from your bank, all items that you have on your person and half of the experience you have gained in any unprotected skills.

If you die to a monster when you have a PK skull you will lose the 10 most valuable stacks of items from your bank, all items that you have on your person and half of the experience you have gained in any unprotected skills.
If you die to a monster when you do not have a PK skull you will lose all of the items on your person except for the 3 most valuable. You will not lose experience or any items from your bank.
What happens when I kill a player in Deadman mode?

When you kill a player you will receive any items they have on their person and you will also be given a key. You can use this key on Deadman chests found in various banks across the map. Within the chest you will
find the 10 most valuable stacks of items from the bank of the player you struck down. From here you will be able to choose the items you would like to keep.

column3: How can I protect my items in Deadman mode?

You can protect up to 10 items by placing them in your safe deposit box. Items in your safe deposit box will not be lost to a player who kills you, unlike those found in your bank. Remember that you can only place 10 single items into your safe deposit box, no stacks.
What are safe zones in Deadman mode?

Safe zones are areas patrolled by very high level guards which can be found in various places across the map. The guards watch out for any player with a PK skull and will attack them if they're spotted. It is still possible to be attacked inside safe zones but the person doing the attacking will not stand a chance of making it out alive.

I am Trobin Arceuus, lord of Arceuus. It's a position I've held for a thousand years, ever since the Ascent of Arceuus.
That's a long time. I guess you've seen quite a bit.
Indeed. I've been present at some of the most notable moments in Kourend's history.
I was there when King Agata IV was deposed, I was there when Kharedst the Builder opened Kourend Castle and I was there when Emperor Imafore was executed.
I tend to keep out of public affairs these days though. My presence is often more of a distraction than a benefit. It also means I can focus on my work in peace.
Your work?
The freeing of souls. There are many souls that find themselves trapped here after death. My people and I do our best to release them.
Tell me about Arceuus.

If you find something magical in Kourend, chances are it came from Arceuus. Our people have lived for a thousand years. The knowledge we've gained in that time has resulted in many a magical discovery.
Most of our discoveries start with the Dark Altar. It is the source of our immortality and our people dedicate their lives to studying it.
Our people also serves an important role in the wider world. We work to free trapped souls so that they may pass on to the next world. It is a crucial task that the Dark Altar helps us to perform.
Was the Dark Altar always here?
Impossible to say. The Dark Altar has been mentioned in records dating back to the earliest days of Kourend. Before then, who knows.
You weren't around back then?
No. The Ascent of Arceuus didn't occur until after Xeric's Age of Strife, hundreds of years after Kourend was formed.
Tell me about the Ascent of Arceuus.
It was a thousand years ago, during the time of King Byrne II. I went to my people and shared the secrets of immortality with them.
Not all of them accepted this gift of course, as was their right. Those that did, were granted new bodies to house their souls. These bodies are sustained by the Dark Altar.
It wasn't you that discovered this secret though was it?
No. It was granted to us by the Tasakaal. They are ancient beings, ones that make us seem like mere children.
Their age and experience have granted them knowledge over life and death that we can only dream of.
The Tasakaal don't like you very much. They called you a liar and claimed you misused the knowledge.
The events that led to the Ascent of Arceuus are more complicated than even the Tasakaal know. But that is a story for another day.
Tell me about your plans.
I had one of my people recover the remains of that device. The one that was absorbing the Dark Altars power.
We're performing tests to see if we can learn more about it. We haven't made any meaningful progress yet though.
Once we've learnt more about it, we'll be in a better position to determine our next move.
I admit, the idea of someone sabotaging the Altar is more than a bit concerning. I hope we can make some progress soon.
Goodbye.

column3: Tell me about the Nightmare.
From the moment I was born, all I ever knew was the Nightmare. Every night she would feast upon us, filling our minds with horrors beyond comprehension.
By day, our warriors would enter her lair in the caves beneath the island. We could not hope to defeat her, we knew that, but our survival was dependent on ensuring she didn't grow too strong.
Here's the thing though. Even now, we know little about her. Before she claimed them, my parents would sometimes tell me a story of her origin.
They told me of a group of shamans who performed an unknown ritual in the hope of gaining great power. The ritual went wrong, though, and instead, they unleashed the Nightmare on this world.
Do you believe the story?
I'm not sure to be honest. I suppose it doesn't matter though. We'll likely never know her true origin. But as long as we can defeat her, we don't need to.
Defeat her? Using the totems?
Exactly. Thanks to the Nightmare, the caves beneath our home are mostly unexplored. There's all sorts of things down there, provided you're brave enough to enter.
I found the totems deep within the caves. Someone far smarter than you or I had worked out how to make them. But they perished before they could use them against her.
I managed to recover them, and with them, we finally drove her off the island.
But she came here.
Yes. And thanks to the Sleeper Plague, she's far stronger than ever before.
Do you know where the Sleeper Plague came from?
No. It was here long before the Nightmare apparently. It resurfaced shortly before she arrived. Probably the work of the vampyres.

The name's Shura. I come from an island called Ashihama, in the Pincers.

It's a group of islands within the Wushanko Isles, a large archipelago to the far east. Over here I think the area is more commonly known as the Eastern Lands.

Back home on the other hand, our numbers equal the humans. Sirens live on pretty much every island in the archipelago.
So why were you the only one to come here?
We took up arms against the Nightmare because we had to, not because we wanted to. We are a peaceful race, and most were all too eager to lay down their weapons once the Nightmare was gone.
So why didn't you?
My kind believe in something called Mo Kal. It means that anything bad that could happen, will happen. The others may have forgotten this, but I have not.
The Nightmare may have left my home, but I won't rest until I know for sure that she can never return.

column3: Tell me about passwords.
Your password is the first line of defence in keeping your account secure.
When choosing a password, make sure to keep it unique. You can do this by using a mix of letters and numbers. You could even use numbers in the middle of your password.
For extra security, you should make sure you use a different password for your account and email.
You should keep your password safe and tell no one. Not even your friends or family.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
Tell me about securing my email.
Make sure you use a separate password for your email account. This will help boost your security and make it less likely for hijackers to steal your account.
You should also enable two-step authentication on your email account, if your email supports it.
This could be done through an authenticator app supplied by your email provider, or it could be done using your mobile phone number.
The type of authenticator changes based on provider, but when active, hijackers will find it hard to access your account. Also, if you get any backup codes, keep them safe.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
Tell me about the authenticator.
The RuneScape authenticator will provide your account with another layer of security against hijackers who might want to steal your account.
As well as requiring a password to enter your account, you will also need a randomly generated number from the authenticator app to login.
You can enable the authenticator by checking your account page on the official RuneScape website.
If you like, I can take you to a useful web page about the RuneScape authenticator.
