To keep your bank secure, you should make sure to set a bank pin. A bank pin is a 4 digit code you will need to put in to access your bank.
It seems I don't have one setup. How do I got about setting up a bank pin?
To setup a bank pin you will need to visit any bank where you can find a banker. You should then speak to the banker and ask them about setting up a bank pin.
After the bank pin has been set, you will need to wait a few days for the pin to take effect.
Thanks, I should go speak to a banker right away.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
Tell me about the Stronghold of Security.
The Stronghold of Security can be found in the Barbarian Village, west of Varrock.
Here you will be tested on your knowledge of account security. You will need to make your way to the bottom floor while answering question on account security and fighting monsters.
Be aware, the deeper into the stronghold you go, the tougher the monster will be. So make sure you bring your best equipment and some food.
If you do manage to make it to the end of each floor, you will be able to loot the chest for some loot. But only once per floor.
If you decide to kill the monsters, you might find they drop some skull sceptre pieces.
Interesting, thanks for the information.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
Can I have a Security book?
Sure thing, here you go.
The Account security tutor hands you a Security book.
Use it well.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
Don't I know you from somewhere?
Ah, you're probably talking about my twin brother who works at the Port Sarim prison.
He spends all his time giving out security books when he could tell you about security instead.
But don't you give out security books too?
Well yes, but at least I tell you about account security as well.
That's true. Maybe I shouldn't be too quick to judge.
Is there anything else you would like to know?
No, thank you.
Come back any time you need any more information on account security.
What ales are you serving?
We serve Crombwick's finest Bloody Bracer, that is all.
Sounds rough, how much?
99 of you finest coins.

column4: Alright, one Bloody Bracer, if that's all you have.
column8: What can you tell me about this town?

column3: Alright, one Bloody Bracer, if that's all you have.
I said 99 coins! You haven't got 99 coins!
Sorry, I'll come back another day.
99 coins? That's ridiculous!
What can I say? The ingredients are locally sourced so it's high quality, I promise.
Well, I guess I shouldn't shoot the messenger.
So...
What can you tell me about this town?
I've not been here long myself, so I'm afraid I may not be of much help.
What happened to the previous barkeep?
Oh, he had to leave.
How come?
Scared of turning.
Turning?
Yes, into a sleeper.
Oh right! You see, for a second there I thought you were talking about vampyres.
Ha ha! We, err, don't see many of those types around here. No, no, not at all.
If you say so.
I do. So...
Actually, I'm no longer thirsty.
Oh, the red thirst will be upon you soon.
Excuse me?
Just a jest, traveller.
Oh.
Hell-
Don't distract me! This formula is highly volatile!
Cool, what are you making?
Ugh, look around you, what does it look like?
A magic potion?! Can I have some?
No, human. This isn't designed for your race, it could have unforeseen consequences.
I can deal with them, I promise.
You can deal with death?
Hmm, perhaps a rain check?
Wise choice. Now please, I'm working a deadline here.
See you around!
Doubtful.
You seem to really enjoy that painting.
Are you alright?
You may speak.
Oh, yes yes, I'm fine.
You look a little beat up.
These scratches? Don't worry, just a disagreement with a thorn bush.
Sure...
Is there something you wanted, bloodbag?
Just looking around.
Well, I'd prefer you did it elsewhere, Crombwick is busy entertaining his guests.
Strange bunch of guests...
Can I go in the Arboretum?
Yes. Now leave me alone.
Human! Get back to the slave pens before I call the guards!
Hello there!
How are you doing in there?
Oh I'm great. Lord Jovkai takes good care of us.
So you don't want to escape?
Why would I want to do that? I'm very happy as I am.
If you say so.
Hey. Leave me be. I'm guardin' this place.
Hello again, Drezel. Is there anything that I can help you out with around here?
Well... I don't think so. There's not much to do in that place.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Nature Spirit quest.
I wouldn't advise going down there before you know the risks, adventurer.
Who are you?
Woo wooo?
Who are you?
Woo wooo!
C'mon, why won't this thing open?
Would you like me to give you a hand with that?
It's okay, I think I've got it... Agh, I thought I had it that time!
Why are you searching this coffin?
I need to bring that mysterious stranger 100 Hallowed marks so that he can help me escape Darkmeyer.
100 seems like a lot. How many do you have so far?
None.
I don't have 100 either.
That's okay. I'm sure I'll get this open eventually.
Hey there! Do you have a grapple I can borrow?
I might have one, but I need it myself. Why do you need a grapple?
I need it to grapple to that pillar over there and get some treasure of course. What else could I need it for?
I mean that makes sense I suppose. How did you end up here?
Well, I made my way to Morytania in search of a place called the Ba... Barlows? I've heard it's a great way to earn gold.
Barrows.
Yeah, that's what I said!
Anyways, I got lost on the way here and was abducted by some vampyres! However, I'm so sneaky I managed to escape and find this place.
The weird hooded guy at the top said that if I get him some hollow marks, he'll help me escape.
You mean Hallowed marks.
Yeah, that's what I said. Don't you listen?
*sigh*
So, can I borrow a grapple?
No, I don't have a grapple on me.
Well, you're clearly a noob then.
C'mon, almost got it...
Having problems?
Agh! You scared me! Now I've lost my lockpick.
Oh, sorry about that. I'm afraid I don't have one for you.
C'mon, almost got it...
Having problems?
Can't you see I'm busy?
Do you have a lockpick?
No and even if I did have one I wouldn't give it to you!
I was just letting you know that having a lockpick helps when getting into these coffins. You appear to be struggling.
Wow, are you okay? What happend to you?
Ugh... Well met, adventurer. I wouldn't go down there if I were you. That trap is an absolute nightmare! The one who created it must be a sadist. I don't know of anyone who has cleared it.

column6: No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?

column3: Oh? I've cleared it.
Oh? Are you pulling my leg, adventurer?
I'm fairly certain that if I did that, it would fall off!
No need to add salt in the wound.
Although I am curious, how did you beat the trap?
I just made sure to prioritise looking out for the arrows. The fire was fairly easy to get through if I just made sure to take one step at a time.
I see, you're clearly more skillful than I. I'm not sure if I'd be agile enough to do that. Do tell, what was on the next floor?

The place looked magnificent, gold lion statues, coffins untouched by anyone else and plenty of Hallowed marks compared to these floors. Although, the traps were significantly harder than the one below.
I see. Well, I guess I'd better brush up on my skills if I want to see it for myself. Nothing worth having in life comes easy right?
That's very true, I wish you the best of luck!
No one has cleared it? How hard can it be?
Well, unlike the rest of the traps I've seen so far, you have to deal with both an arrow trap and a fire trap at the same time.
Wow, that does sound hard. Do you have any tips for me?
Well, individually they aren't that hard to do. The fires are always swapping between on and off. I think that if you run to where the fire just was you should be safe.
The hardest part for me is the arrows. You have to look forward to watch the fire trap whilst also looking over your shoulder to see where the arrows are.
I certainly wish there was a way to see both at once. Perhaps it would help if a fellow adventurer was looking down from above to call out where the arrows are.
Yeah... I'd imagine having an aerial view of the situation would be pretty helpful.
Of course, but we both know that's impossible for one person! Ouch! Sorry, it hurts to laugh. I wish you luck adventurer!
Would you like some help?
Urgh, it just happened again! Every time I almost have it my hand slips.
Oh, that's unfortunate. Are you using a lockpick?
Yes. Well actually, I'm using a Strange old lockpick. I found it while looting one of these coffins and I typically have better luck with it.
Oh, that's interesting. I'll keep my eyes out for one.
I've found a few of them while raiding this place. There appear to be more of them on this floor than the floors above.
I see. If you don't mind me asking, you already have dark graceful so why are you still looking for hallowed marks?
Oh, it's because of this little fellow following me. I've heard that the Dark acorn sold by the guy upstairs will transform him into a Dark Squirrel.
Wow, I didn't know that! That sounds pretty cool.
Yeah, that's what I thought but that mysterious stranger is asking for 3,000 Hallowed marks for it.
3,000? That sounds extortionate!
Yeah, that's what I thought. Feels like he set the price just to keep me down here for longer. Still, it's not like I have anything better to do.
I see, well best of luck. Hopefully you survive long enough to finish your goal.
I'm sure I'll be fine.
You new here? I don't recognise you.
So... tired...
You're not one of the slaves assigned to this mine! Get back to the pens!
What are you drinking?
Blood!
How are you getting drunk on blood?
They keep some of the tithes drunk all the time and then take it from them.
How very creative.
I know right! Bloody brilliant!
I don't want whatever it is you're selling.
But I'm not selling anything.
You think I believe that? Why else would you be here?
Just seeing the sights?
What sights? What's wrong with you.
Nothing...
Get out, you weirdo!
Who are you?
Get out of my house!
But I...
But nothing! Get out!
Hey there. Have you seen Frank?
Frank?
Yes, Frank. He's my pet bloodveld. He runs off a lot so I was wondering if you'd seen him.
Frank doesn't seem like a very fitting name for a bloodveld.
Oh, he was named after my last pet. That one wasn't a bloodveld though, that one was a human.
You had a pet human?
Yes! A pet human called Frank.
Frank was great. He died though. Mother said it was my fault, that I didn't feed him properly. I'm not allowed pet humans now.
It's okay though. Now I have Frank the bloodveld. He's great. I don't need to feed him. He feeds himself.
What a nice happy ending.
Player: Hello there.
Darling, who's this?
I don't know, darling. Why don't you ask them?
Yes, good idea!
Who are you?
Hello there!
Draynar? Any connection to Draynor?
Oh yes. The Draynar family has been around since before vampyres came to this world.
Over time, some people took the name and started pronouncing it differently. Hence Draynor.
Draynor is more commonly used as a first name though, with Draynar as a last name.
Thanks for the information. I wonder if there's a Draynor Draynar out there.
Now that would be funny.
See you around.
Who are you? Why are you in my home?
The tithes are growing weak. That werewolf needs to do a better job of keeping them fed.
What do you feed them?
There's no shortage of corpses around here. The dead can still have some uses.
You're feeding them corpses? No wonder they're becoming weak. That meat must have all sorts of problems.
What else would you have me feed them? If I give them nicer food, I'm wasting more money than if I were to just kill them and buy some more.
I... I suppose.
Yes?
What are you selling?
Lanterns. Want one?
Yes please.
Why are you selling lanterns?
It's dark around here.
You make a very valid point.
Yes. Want one?
No thanks.
Suit yourself.
Looking to trade?
What have you got?
Take a look.
No thanks.
Then we have nothing more to discuss.
Yes?
What are you serving?
Blood.
Is that it?
Yes, by the pint. Now, do you want one or not?
Sure.
Two coins.
Oh dear, I don't seem to have enough money.
Clear off then.
I'll pass.
Clear off then.
Looking for a bit of meat?
I beg your pardon?
Meat! We've got all the good stuff here.

column6: Why do you have all this meat?

column3: Show me what you've got.
Why do you have all this meat?
Some prefer solids to go with their blood. That, and the werewolf visitors need something to eat too.
Where does it all come from?
Look around you! There's no shortage of meat in these parts.
You know what, I think I've heard enough.
Whatever you say. So, want some meat?
I'm good, thanks.
Come back if you ever want some meat!
Now you look like a vyre in need of some new threads.
Let's trade.
Do I?
Oh yes. And luckily for you, I have everything you could ever need. Clothes, or the materials to make them if that's more your thing. All pre-scented as well.
Pre-scented?
Oh don't go acting like you don't know what I mean. You've done a decent job, but behind that scent, I can tell you're just a lowly vyre.
Fear not, I am no judge. I know that there are many like you who want a taste of upper class life. That's why all my outfits are scented. Helps you fit right in.
Does it not bother you having lower class vampyres up here?
Me? No. As long as you've got money, I don't care who you are.
Fair enough.
So, want to take a look?
I'm fine, thanks.
I'll be here if you change your mind.
Good day sir. Could I interest you in one of our finest Bloody Bracers? It's a local speciality.
One Bloody Bracer please.
That will be 99 coins.
I don't have that much.
Then for now, our business is at an end.
What happened to Carl?
Carl?
The old barkeep.
Oh yes, Carl!
He had to leave I'm afraid. Fear not though. I have taken over things here.
And you are?
Roy is the name. Now, could I interest you in one of our finest Bloody Bracers?
I'm not thirsty.
Then for now, our business is at an end.
What's going on?
Speaking would certainly help your case.
Well, okay then.
Hello.
Not infected are you?
I don't think so.
You don't seem very sure. We don't want any infected near the children. Be off with you!
Hello.
Mother says I shouldn't speak with strangers.
Fair enough.
Hello mortal. Have you come to retrieve something you lost when you died?

column8: Yes, have you got anything for me?

column3: How does that work?
When you die, you often drop things you were carrying. In most cases, a gravestone appears near where you died, and your items can be retrieved there.
However, gravestones do not last for long. When your gravestone collapses, your items come here, to me. I can return them to you - though I charge a fee for my services.
Aside from that, if you bring me your unwanted possessions, and sacrifice them into my Coffer here, I'll count their value against any future fees I charge you.
I don't accept just any junk, but I'll try to give you a good price for anything decent.
So do you need to retrieve something you lost when you died?
What is this place?
As you should be able to see, I am Death. The Grim Reaper. The Inexorable One. The Inescapable Grasp of Mortal Destiny. And this is my little office. Nice, isn't it?

column6: Your decorations leave a bit to be desired.

column3: It's lovely.
Thank you. I feel the colour scheme suits my style. Now, can I help you retrieve something you lost when you died?
Your decorations leave a bit to be desired.
Sometimes it's hard to care for beauty when one's very existence is just seen as a curse upon the world. Now, do you actually want to retrieve something from me?
Yes, have you got anything for me?

column4: Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?
column6: Can I change how I die?

column3: Can I choose a different-looking gravestone?
Er... I suppose so.
How would you like to... die?
Not just now, thanks.
Really? There isn't much else for you to do here. But you know your business.
What do you want?

column4: Who are you and what are you doing?
column8: What's with the glowing portal thing?

column3: I'm Vicks, squire to Sir Culler Flife. He's away on a surveillance mission to Burthorpe, so he sent me down here to do some cleaning.

column4: You don't seem to be cleaning much.
column6: What's your master doing in Burthorpe?
column10: What's with the glowing portal thing?

column3: Don't tell the knights, but I'm just not in the mood for it! I've served for years, and worked really hard, but they're not even thinking of making me a knight.
I don't know what the problem is. At my last review, I heard the examiner muttering something about my name, but I've no idea what he meant by that.
Keeping an eye on those Imperial Guard. We can't trust 'em, you know. But I shouldn't talk about his mission.

column6: What's with the glowing portal thing?

column3: Tell me about this place.
This place? It's the castle crypt. The greatest White Knights are buried here, after a lifetime in the service of Saradomin. At least, that's how it used to be.
When I was a new recruit, they brought me here and told me that if I served Saradomin faithfully, and with distinction, maybe I'd earn the honour of burial in this place too.
But if you think about it, that's never going to happen - there just isn't space for more tombs! Anyway, my plan is to avoid dying, and maybe marry one of the barmaids when I retire.
What's with the glowing portal thing?
It's because of something the Temple Knights have, called the Gaze of Saradomin. They get the option of being brought to Falador when they die, so Death has to maintain a presence in the area.
That portal takes you to Death's own realm. He's got portals in all the places where people go when they die - Lumbridge, Edgeville and the rest. I hate it - the thing's terrifying!
I'll leave you alone.
Hello, how are you doing?
I'm good thank you, how can I help you today?

column6: How many laps have I done?

column3: What is this place?
This is our agility course, we use it to stay nimble and to keep our wits sharp. My name is Bobawu and I look after the course.
As a friend and fellow monkey, you're free to use it anytime, but you'll need to be as nimble as a ninja first!
Oh great, thank you.
Are there any rewards you can offer me?
Could you tell me how many laps I've completed?
I can't offer you anything for now, so I don't see much reason to count your laps either.
You need to complete Monkey Madness 2 for Bobawu to offer rewards and to count your lap total
What can you offer me?
I can't offer you anything for now, so I don't see much reason to count your laps either.
You need to complete Monkey Madness 2 for Bobawu to offer rewards and to count your lap total
On second thought, never mind.
That's okay my friend, come back anytime.
Hello there.
Aye? Who's that, what do you want?

column6: Can you teach me about canoes?

column3: Who are you?
Marten.
Oh, straight to the point.
I got betta' things to do than waste my time talkin' to you.
You're rather rude aren't you?
Fine, wanna know more 'bout canoes?
No thanks, not from you at least.
Then get out of here and stop botherin' me.
Could you teach me about canoes?
Hahaha! Sorry mate, you'll not be able to make any canoes outta that tree there. You'll need to get a bit more skilled at the craft of Woodcuttin'.
But once you get a bit betta', you'll be able to make a canoe and ride the river.
Welcome wanderer.

column6: What can you do for me?

column3: What is this place?
You're surrounded by a relic of a long lost kingdom.
What happened here?
Oh, I couldn't really tell you that.
This place has sat in ruin for an age, slowly destroyed by the harsh climate of the Wilderness.
If it's a ruin, what's the point in being here?
I search for knowledge. I want to know what happened to this part of the world.
Whilst looking for answers, I slowly turned this broken town into a safe haven for travellers. Welcome to Ferox Enclave.
Quite a dangerous place for a town, don't you think?
It is, but that's why it's needed! Look around, you can see how many others share my opinion.
You'll find yourself quite safe inside my enclave - the protective barriers should keep any troublemakers out.
I will warn you though, if you've had Teleblock cast upon you, I will not allow you back into the Enclave. You'd be a danger to the others gathered here.

column4: What can you do for me?

column3: Thanks for the information! I'll take a look around.
Tread carefully my friend.
What can you do for me?
Well, if you'd like, I can make it so you respawn in our Enclave. It'll put you right in the heart of all the chaos that surrounds us.
Tell me more.
This is how it'll work: When you die, you'll respawn right here in Ferox Enclave, just outside the pub we've set up. You will lose your items as normal of course.
I won't be able to do anything if you die somewhere like Castle Wars or the Emir's Arena; they have their own magic to keep you safe.
It'll cost you though! Transporting you here is no easy task. 5 million coins should do it, that'd be a one time fee of course.
I don't have that much money on me.
Understandable, you'd have to be a brave man to be carrying that much gold out here.
That doesn't interest me.
Come find me if you change your mind.
Never mind, I'm just looking around.
So be it.
Hello!
Can I help you?
I was just curious as to what you do around here.
I protect other travellers from monsters, both animal and human kind.
Human? Can't say I've seen many human shaped monsters in the Wilderness.
When you've been in the Wilderness as long as I have, you learn that not all monsters show themselves on the outside.
Uhm... alright then, I'll leave you to your duties.
Watch yourself out there, it can be hard to tell friend from foe in these lands.
What brings you all the way out into the Wilderness?
The hunt.
Oh... you partake in that?
Not the hunt for other beings! The hunt for knowledge.
Knowledge? Can't say I've seen much of that around here. In case you didn't notice, it's all ruins.
Maybe for someone like you, but to us followers of Zamorak, there's relics of his mighty power everywhere.
Isn't it a little dangerous to be looking for knowledge out here?
That doesn't bother us. Our lord will protect us, we hunt in service of him.
I'll leave you to it then.
Eyup. They call me Skully. I run this Wilderness Loot Chest. What can I do for you?
Well, you know how when you kill someone all of their stuff just ends up in a pile on the floor and it's really hard to pick it all up quickly?
Actually, I've never killed anyone else.
...Oh. Well, when you do, all of their stuff just ends up in a pile on the floor and it's really hard to pick it all up quickly.
Wow, didn't expect to find a scientist out here.
I'm out here on a mission, do you think I chose to hang around these lowlifes?
I'm not one to judge.
What is this 'mission' you mentioned?
I'm out here to conduct research, I've been told a giant spider lurks in the heart of the Wilderness.
Her venom is priceless and it would aid me greatly in my research.
Research? What could you possibly want with a giant spider's venom?
Venenatis is the last of her kind. Lots of giant spiders used to dwell deep in the mountains until the savage dwarves killed them all.
She is the last one left and I must have a sample of her venom.
What I want with the specimen however, is none of your business!
Woah sorry, didn't mean to touch a nerve. Fighting a giant spider sounds like a great idea.
I've tried to put it off for as long as I could, but this is the final component needed for my research.
Then what are you waiting around here for? Go out there and fight her.
You look ready for combat.
Aye, indeed I am.
What brings you to this place? I can't imagine anyone coming here by choice.
You're right, I did not come here by choice. I came here for vengeance.
Vengeance? Against whom? Did someone take your gardening equipment?
My mission is not against another man and I will not have it mocked.
Okay, sorry, I was just trying to lighten the mood. Care to tell me what it is against then?
Callisto, the great bear of the wilderness.
Can't say I've come across it before.
I'm not surprised, you'd do well to avoid him. Callisto is a great bear, his strength and size enhanced by the corruption of the Wilderness.
Well met, fellow adventurer.
Adventurer? I am no mere Adventurer, I am Andros Mai, brother of the Holy Order of Saradomin. You would do well to greet me with respect.
Andros Mai? Sorry, but I can't say I've heard of you I'm afraid.
I wouldn't have expected someone of your... stature to know of me.
Tell me, what do you know of the vile Vet'ion?
Nothing, but I have a feeling you're about to fill me in.
Oh great, another customer. What do you want?

column4: I'd like to access my bank account, please.
column6: I'd like to check my PIN settings.
column10: What are you doing out here?

column3: What are you doing out here?
I used to work in the East Varrock branch. Then a request came in to set up a bank in this new town.
The other clerks and myself pulled straws and I was unlucky enough to be sent to this stinking death trap.
Now I'm stuck here, ferrying items back and forth to the bank's safe in Varrock for people like you.
That doesn't sound very fun, but you're doing a great service for us adventurers.
Tell that to my back and legs, I'm exhausted from carrying all this junk back and forth.
Hand me a banknote, and I'll try to convert it to an item.
Welcome my friend to the Old Nite! What can I do for you?

column6: Your pub looks a bit rough.

column3: Got anything strong to drink?
Of course I do! I can offer you a big tasty beer, yours for only two coins.
Oh dear, I don't seem to have enough money.
No worries, there's a bank just around the corner if you want to grab some coin.
Your pub looks a bit rough.
It's all part of the aesthetic! Adventurers who've just returned from the fight of their lives don't want a fancy la-de-da establishment like you'd find down south.
They want somewhere to relax and have some hearty ale.
And that's what you offer with your broken tables and glass covered floors?
Aye it is, because here at the Old Nite, your safety is our lowest priority!
Just browsing...
Hey, how can I help you?
What do you do here?
This is one of the branches for Mahogany Homes, Gielinor's first construction company.
Oh wow, how can I get involved?
If you go see Amy in the Falador branch, she'll fill you in. Her office is just east of the Estate Agent in Falador.
Nice, thank you.
Please excuse me, I'm rather busy.
What brings you here, young man?
I'm just wandering around.
Oh, that's nice. I used to wander around, back when my legs were better. So long ago.
Nothing, really.
That's the trouble with young people these days. Not my boy, though. He's a good boy, always working. That's why he never visits. Run along now, young man.
Oh, you have returned. I have cancelled your current assignment; I do not feel Morytania to be a suitable place for you to slay.
Hello! Who are you?
Hello there. I'm the Leagues Assistant. I help the Leagues Tutor out. You'll find him just outside of Lumbridge Castle if you want to speak to him.
You can find the Leagues Tutor by looking for his icon on your map.
Okay, thanks.
Do you want to buy any fine clothes? Or would you like your scythe back?
Hello. Who are you?
The name's Gordon. Good day to you.
It's a nice farm you've got here.
Thank you. We built it ourselves.
Really? So you haven't been here long?
Nope. Not too long ago you couldn't safely travel around these parts. Too many lizardmen. But then some Hosidius explorers discovered how fertile this land was.
Lord Hosidius made a deal with Lord Shayzien and the lizardmen were cleared out to make room for the Farming Guild.
When we heard, we decided to come up here and start up our own farm.

column6: Very nice. Well I hope it goes well for you.

column3: Need a hand with anything?
Very nice. Well I hope it goes well for you.
Thank you friend. See you later.
Hello there. Is this your home?
It is. What brings you here?
I'm just looking around.
Well you won't find anything too exciting here I'm afraid. Just farming.
Well you have fun with it.
Wotcha guv'na!
Hey! Talk to me if you want to know anything worth knowing.
Best talk to his highness over there, 'fore he goes gettin' upset.
Excuse me, what is this place?
What is this place? This is Soul Wars, a glorious battleground where you must fight to crush the souls of your enemies!
Really? Are souls easy to crush?
Easier than you'd imagine.
I see. So how does it all work?
I can give you a demonstration if you're interested?

column3: What did you do before you came here?
I worked in a chapel dedicated to our lord, Saradomin. My task was to light the chapel candles, but I couldn't reach them myself and I kept getting dazzled by the light whenever I tried.
I'd call adventurers from across the world, summoning them to my chapel to do the task for me. I needed them to light the tall candles, but not the short ones.
However, adventurers got confused, and thought they should light the short candles as well as the tall candles, so I made them try again. And again.
Eventually my chapel was closed down. They said I'd trapped adventurers there for too long. All I wanted was for them to light the tall candles without lighting the short candles!
Anyway, now I live here, and remember the good old days. It is nice to meet you, {name}.
So your name is Pete?
Yes, it is a common name. I also know of Party Pete, Parroty Pete, Postie Pete, Pirate Pete, Petrified Pete and 'Picarron' Pete. The Makeover Mage has used the name Pete too.

Get yerself a harpoon from the crate on the ship, then go fish around the island t' catch some harpoonfish. They make fer fine ammo against Tempoross!
Once ye caught some, ye can cook 'em at the shrines on the island if ye want 'em to pack more of a punch. Then come back t' the ship an' load 'em in the ammunition crates next to the cannons.
Our cannoneers will get t' firin' the harpoonfish at Tempoross. When it's weak an' submerges to recover its energy, get down to the jetty next t' the ship an' fish those spirit pools.

Be quick with fishin' those spirit pools though, or it'll come back so strong we'll have to abandon the fight! With any luck, we'll weaken those spirit fish enough t' subdue Tempoross. Now get t' the fight, sailor!
Aye aye!

If Tempoross electrocutes a cannon t' stop it from firin', ya better load your harpoonfish into the other ammunition crates t' keep them cannons firin' instead.

Also, make sure t' grab a rope from the ship crates an' keep an eye out for big waves. We'll make sure t' shout about them. Then ye best quickly tether yerself t' an island totem pole or ship mast with that rope.
If the waves break the totem pole or ship mast, ye can grab a hammer from the ship crates t' fix 'em up before the next big wave hits.
Oh, an' keep an eye out for lightnin' clouds causin' fires. Get a bucket from the ship crates, fill it with water at a pump, and get t' puttin it out before it spreads.
If ye get hit by the waves or fire, don't be surprised when ye lose those fish an' tools ye gathered. Now get t' the fight, sailor!

Camdozaal is a shadow of what it once was. We Imcando Dwarves were the finest artisans in the world, but now I am all that remains. Today, you'll only find echoes of our once great city.

Barronite. You'll only find it in these ruins. If you can gather some for me, I can use it to keep the Forge lit. In return, I'll let you take what you want from our Great Vault.
I no longer have use for anything in the Vault. Besides, material possessions mean nothing compared to the fire of the Sacred Forge.

Ah... It's a tough tale to tell. Even though it's been many years since the last of my kin died out, the memory is still fresh.
You don't have to tell me if the memory hurts too much.
No, I will. The legacy of my kin must live on.
As you can see around you, Camdozaal was once a great city. Alive with the hum of activity. We dug deep into the mountain and reaped the rewards.
Our methods would often differ from other dwarves. Whereas they just used traditional smithing techniques, we would combine them with magic as well.
Alas, that was ultimately our undoing. We learned of a horde of barbarians pillaging across the land, hunting down and killing anyone who dared use magic.
We underestimated them. We believed our weapons would be enough to keep us safe. We were wrong.
The barbarians brought ruin upon Camdozaal. Most of my kind died as the city collapsed around them. Only a few of us survived until the end. Now, only I remain.
The world has changed a lot, Ramarno. Magic is practiced freely. Those barbarians failed to wipe it from Gielinor.
I'm glad they didn't win, I suppose. But it doesn't change much for me. I am still the last Imcando Dwarf.
I'm sorry Ramarno. I will do my best to help ensure the legacy of your kin lives on.

column3: How do I play board games?
You can challenge someone to a game anywhere in the Games Zone (except on a PvP or Deadman world) by using the right click option.
Choose the type of game and then choose the options you want such as time per move.
If your opponent accepts the challenge you will be taken to one of the tables around where you will play your game of choice.
Once you have finished your game you will come back here where you can challenge again! We also have tables in a few pubs around the world!
What games can I play?
Currently we offer Draughts, Runelink, Runesquares, and Runeversi.
Draughts?
Draughts uses standard rules, apart from: a draw is declared if no piece has been taken or promoted for forty moves.
Runelink?
Yup, you have to get four runes in row.
Runesquares?
Yes, you take it in turns to add a line with the goal of making squares. Everytime you make a square you take another turn.
Runeversi?
Yep, the aim is to have more of your runes on the board than your opponent. You can take your opponents pieces by trapping them between your own.

column3: What is a clan?
Ah, clans. Where do I begin? Clans are groups of people gathered together for numerous reasons. Usually they have shared interests, like activities they enjoy together.
These activities could include improving certain skills, battling the same monsters, or even battling other clans!
Other clans form together because they just enjoy the company of other like-minded people. The clan community can be a great resource if you should ever need help with anything.

column4: How do I join a clan?
column6: What can a clan offer me?

column3: How do I join a clan?
You can either form your own clan with your friends, or apply to an already existing clan.
Should you choose to form your own clan you will need four friends to join you, and it is recommended that you have spent a good amount of time in this world first. Leadership is not for everyone.
However, fret not. There are plenty of interesting and exciting clans out there! Check out the clan recruitment board to see which clans are currently accepting applications.
You can either form your own clan with your friends, or apply to an already existing clan.
What can a clan offer me?
Clans offer you the ability to have an official gathering of friends or like-minded individuals in a hierarchical structure.
In other words, you and your friends get an exclusive chat channel and a Clan Hall, as well as the ability to assign ranks to members.
Ranks can be assigned from custom pre-sets, which then determine what permissions that person has.
For example: One person may have the rank to kick players from the chat, while another has the rank to access the Clan Coffer.

column10: I'm in a clan. Can you give me anything?

column3: What is the Clan Coffer?
The Clan Coffer is a shared coin store, used by members of the clan. Highly ranked members can assign who has permission to deposit and withdraw coins.
What is a Clan Hall?

A Clan Hall is a private area only accessible for the people with the permission to enter. High ranked members of the clan can restrict it to only allow certain ranks in, or open it up to even allow guests.
Why would I need a Clan Hall? Can't I get a house instead?
The beauty of it is that you can have both. You can keep your house for private guests and your own personal use, but when you wish to see larger groups then the Clan Hall may be more fitting.

My mission is to administer clans; I help form them and can tell you anything you need to know about them.

The Royal Guard was established by King Byrne I. He felt that it was dangerous for Shayzien House to control the only military in the kingdom, so he decided to establish a small one of his own.
Ever since then, the Royal Guard have served Kourend's ruler.

Tell me about the Kourend Council.
Kourend's last King, Kharedst IV, had only one child when he died. She was too young to take the throne, so the Kourend Council was formed to look after things until she came of age.
Alas, she was very close to her father and his sudden death drove her to insanity. With no suitable ruler, the Kourend Council was made permanent.
How is the Council structured?
The Kourend Council is made up of four councillors. Every four years there is an election for the people to decide who the councillors should be.
One of the councillors holds the position of Head Councillor and this rotates every year. I am the current Head Councillor.
The other councillors are Councillor Hughes, Councillor Unkar and Councillor Orson.
So where do the five houses fit in?

The five houses of Kourend each have their own leader who rules over their city. The leaders of the individual houses must enforce and obey the laws set out by the Kourend Council, but can otherwise rule as they see fit.

Most citizens of Shayzien are part of the Shayzien Army in some form or other. We are responsible for defending Kourend against external and internal threats.
What are the current threats against Kourend?
Externally, we have recently being dealing with increased lizardman activity. We've also been keeping a close eye on Varlamore to the south, just in case they try anything.
Internally, we have seen a rise in gang crime across the kingdom. It seems to be especially prevalent in Port Piscarilius.
How do you tackle these issues?
By doing what we do best citizen. There's no threat that can't be defeated by a Shayzien soldier with a sword in their hand.
Anything else I can help you with citizen?
Tell me about your plans.
Our war plans? I'm afraid most of that is confidential.
What I can tell you is that our main focus right now is the lizardman threat. We've moved a great number of troops into the Kebos Lowlands to combat the issue.
Is that going well?
Absolutely, we've pushed the lizardmen back to the point where we're finally able to allow citizens such as yourself into the region.
Anything else I can help you with citizen?
Goodbye.
Farewell citizen.
Hello.
Hello there.
Tell me about yourself.
I am Kandur Hosidius and I am the lord of Hosidius, the city of farmers and chefs. I live here with my wife, Elena, and my two sons, Artur and Pandur.
My family and I have a peaceful existence here. That's mainly because I care not for the politics of the other houses. I instead devote my time to more meaningful pursuits.
Such as?
Ensuring that Kourend is well fed. We may live in gentle times now but who knows how long it will be that way. Sooner or later another war or long winter will hit us. History has proven that.
Anything else I can help you with?
Tell me about Hosidius.
Hosidius is home to the farmers and chefs of Kourend. We are the main food supplier to the kingdom and we ensure that her people are fed.
We also own more land than the other Kourend houses. We need the extra space for all of our crops.
Do the other houses not get annoyed at how much land you have?
Sometimes. They know it is necessary though. There was once a time when the land was shared equally. But then the great famine came, and Kourend did not have the food to last through it.
After that, more space was given to Hosidius. We've had the most land ever since.
Anything else I can help you with?
Tell me about your plans.
Plans? My only plan is to keep providing food to this kingdom.
But what of the Royal Accord of Twill? You must have kept it for a reason.
I did. The Accord has the potential to be a powerful weapon, for words cut deeper than a blade ever can. However, I have no need to use this weapon, not unless the other houses give me reason to.
Anything else I can help you with?
Goodbye.
Until next time.
...and he says that it's of the greatest urgency.
Greatest urgency? I don't like urgency. This is quite simply not on.
Hiya!
Who is this human, Councillor Unkar? What are they doing here?
I'm afraid I don't know.
Oh. Could you make them go away?
Sorry human. We're currently engaging in important official business. You'll need to come back another time.
What do you want?

column3: Who are you?
What? Everyone knows who I am. I'm Pandur Hosidius, son of Lord Kandur Hosidius. You know him? The man who owns all this land? Well I'm his son.
What are these farming patches for?
This is our vinery. My father's cracked the secret of viticulture, and although our climate's too cold for most grapes, we've made a working vineyard here.
Don't get any ideas, though. We're not having just any random stranger wander in off the fields and try to grow grapes.
Have you been drinking?
I've got to test the produce. Ever since I was a child, I've been the official tester for the bacon, the beef, the pies, the beer, everything. Now there's wine!
* BURP *
I'll leave you to it.
Good day to you.

Nilsal, {name}. It is good to see you.
Likewise, my Queen. How have things been since the Emissaries were dealt with?
Well, with the cult out of the way, we've been able to refocus on the recent opening of the kingdom. Signing the treaties was only the first step.
There are new opportunities for us in areas such as trade that we're still yet to fully explore.
Then of course you have Kourend. The complicated history between our kingdoms means we are yet to sign a treaty with them, but my hope is that will change soon.
Can't stop to talk human. Lady Lovakengj might need me.
Yesss?
You can speak!?
Of courssse, sssome of usss remember the high ssspeech out old massster ssspoke in.

Yesss, we ssspeak the language of war far better. It isss the only way we know of.
This master you speak of...
I know only what my eldersss passssed down. Very little.
How long ago since this master left you?
Many generationsss have come and gone sssince he walked amongssst usss.
Do you remember his name?
K'uhul ajaw isss the name we ssspeak. You manfolk ssspeak a different name.
Hmmm...
Why are you down here?
Thisss isss our temple, we don't usssually get many visssitorsss... We make sssacrifice, offeringsss to our massster.
What kind of... sacrifices?
Thisss and that. Whatever out massster desssiresss.
This master you speak of...
Nevermind, bye.
Ye niauh, human.

You travel all the way out to Shayzien just for a few beers? Don't you have a pub back home?

Have you ever been in there? Such a rowdy crowd... people shouting across the bar about 'Farming this', 'Farming that'... can barely hear myself think half the time.
No, no... Can't be doin' with it. That's why I make the trip out here for a nice quiet one.
Well I'd better leave you to it then!
Not often you see a couple of soldiers out for a drink.
We've just finished our first duties in the Lizardman Canyon. A few drinks at the Cloak and Stagger to celebrate is always traditional.
Sounds like you earned it. Enjoy!
'Ow yer doin', pal?
Just passing through, thanks. Are you feeling okay?
N... Never been better!
Just making sure... You seem a little unsturdy on your feet there.
I like you, mate. We've really c-*hic*-connected. You're like a brother to me.
You see any of those lizards 'round here, you give me a shout. I'll show 'em. Smash 'em.
I'm going to go now.
Hello, are you interested in our agility training courses?
Yes, is it difficult?
Nothing is difficult for a Shayzien soldier. If you do the training every day, you can be as good as us.
No thanks.
Fair enough. Feel free to give it a go if you change your mind.
I'm looking for a quest!
In this holy place I can only offer you calm and peace.
Calm and Peace? Sounds like the quest for me! How should I start?
Yes, calm and peace. Just stay here with me and you will feel it eventually.
Oh... well... thank you.
Hello, you look worried.
My husband is serving near the Lizardman Canyon. I'm worried that something might happen to him.
And I lost my job last week. I need to find another one before my savings run out.
Oh, that is bad. I'm sorry to hear that.
Well, it's a difficult time for a lot of people I guess. The war with the lizardmen never ends.
Hello. Can you give me any farming advice?
Can't you see I'm busy?
Oh, sorry. I thought you might be able to help me with farming like other gardeners.

Well guessed, adventurer.

column6: How do you feel about this place?

column3: Are you from Lovakengj?
You are wrong this time, adventurer. I'm actually from Ice Mountain.
I always wanted to visit Lovakengj to see the Blast Mine. This year I finally saved up enough to travel here.
However, the war with the lizardmen means Lovakengj is dangerous to get to from here. I'll need to go the long way round.
What do you think about this place?
To be honest, Shayzien is a bit boring for visitors. It's all about war and military things.
The only place I would recommend is the Cloak and Stagger. You'll find some pretty good drinks there.
See you later.
Hello there.
Hello traveller, do you know what this is?
It looks like a monument.
Yes. I served in the military for 30 years. This monument always reminds me of my days in the army.
Hello there.
Good day to you.
Who are you?
I'm Commissioner Anwar. I'm in charge of the Shayzien Constabulary. With Lord Shayzien currently busy with the war efforts, I'm also assisting him with his duties here in the city.
What's the Shayzien Constabulary?

The Shayzien Army is split into six regiments plus the Shayzien Constabulary. While the six regiments are jointly responsible for protecting Kourend from external threats, we deal with issues closer to home.
What are the six regiments?

The Intelligence Corps, the Medical Corps, the Engineering Corps, the Logistics Corps, the Rangers and of course, the Infantry. Each regiment is led by a general who reports directly to Lord Shayzien.
It feels like there must be a bit of overlap between the Constabulary and the regiments, especially the Intelligence Corps.
On paper we're totally separate from the regiments. However, in reality you are correct. The distinction between internal and external threats grows murkier by the day.
More and more we find ourselves working alongside the Intelligence Corps and the other regiments. In particular, they've been supporting us in combating the rising gang threat in Port Piscarilius.
What is this place?
This is the Shayzien Administration. The city of Shayzien is run from here.
It seems very quiet.
A lot of focus right now is on the war with the lizardmen. Most senior members of the Shayzien Army, including Lord Shayzien himself, are working out of the Shayzien Encampment instead.
So the Shayzien Army are also responsible for running the city?
Indeed. There's more of a separation between the city of Shayzien and the Shayzien Army now than there used to be, but this will likely always be a military settlement.
See you later.
Hello there, I'm Captain Bruce. Do you want to serve in the Shayzien Army and defend our kingdom?
Yes, I'd love to join.
Wonderful! To get started, you need to answer a few questions.
Are you a resident of Kourend?
Errrr... Not really.
Ah. Then you cannot join I'm afraid.
How come?
It's in the rules I'm afraid. Only citizens of Kourend are allowed to join the Shayzien Army.
Is that not too restrictive?
Well at one time only citizens of Shayzien could join the army. It wasn't until the reign of King Byrne I that people from other parts of the kingdom were allowed to enlist.
Of course, many people in Kourend still like to stick to tradition. After all, the five cities of Kourend have always had very defined roles within the kingdom.
Interesting. So most people in the army are still from Shayzien?
Indeed. While the Shayzien Army is by far the largest military force in Kourend, the other cities still have some form of militia, apart from Arceuus of course.
Even if someone from elsewhere in the kingdom wants to become a soldier, they're far more likely to join their local city force than come to us.
Still, times are slowly changing. Every year we see more people from outside Shayzien enlist.
I see. Thanks for the information.
My pleasure.
No, I'm not interested.
That's alright. Come back if you change your mind.
Ah, hello! Isn't it a wonderful day?
You seem happy.
And why wouldn't I be? I'm part of the best fighting force in the world! The Shayzien Army!
The best?
Of course!
So the Shayzien Army has no weaknesses at all?

Well... I suppose we don't really have any magical capabilities. That's more an Arceuus thing. Though of course, they're mostly pacifists. Apparently they didn't even properly fight in the War of the Five Houses.
Still, I guess 'War of the Four Houses while House Arceuus watched' isn't as catchy a name.
Right... But apart from magic, the Shayzien Army has no weaknesses?
Well... we are just an army. We don't have a navy, so can't really deal with any threats at sea. Lady Piscarilius is meant to be in charge of the Kourend Navy. Problem is, it doesn't actually exist.
How come?
Lady Piscarilius has little interest in that sort of thing. Lord Shayzien wants to establish a Shayzien Navy instead, but there's a lot of pushback from the rest of the kingdom.
They worry about Shayzien having too much power. It does mean we'll have big problems against any enemy navy, but on their heads be it I suppose.
Anyway, apart from those minor issues, the Shayzien Army has absolutely no weaknesses!
If you say so. See you later.
Goodbye!
Hello friend.
Hello, what are you doing here?
My name is Jessie. I help look after the forest.
Nice to meet you. You must know this area very well then.
I do. There're all sorts of interesting creatures around here. Be careful, some of them are not very friendly. A lot of travellers have become their victims.
I see. Thanks for the warning.
No problem! Safe travels my friend.

Adventurer? No. I'm a natural historian from Varrock. I'm working on a project to research the creatures of Kourend.
Don't you think this place is so fascinating? It looks like this cave is a major habitat for the giants.
Yeah, there are many different giants here for sure. How did you manage to get this far? Those giants are quite hostile to visitors.
Well, I just ran past them as fast as I could.
Anyway, I'd better get back to my research.
Sorry, but only guards are allowed up there.

The Wintertodt, or the Winter beast as it was often known at the time, terrorised northern Kourend for five decades.
Logios is currently studying the Wintertodt Invasion, and we have various texts from that era.
Is there something else I can help you with?
What can you tell me about Mount Quidamortem?
Our first records of the mountain date back to the 36th decade where a Shayzien patrol discovered the mountain during a survey of the Kebos Lowlands.
King Shayzien VII was keen on conquering more land for Kourend and demanded his people explore suitable territories.
The mountain became known as Mount Quidamortem after it was realised venturing towards the summit resulted in certain death.

Gnosi is our expert on Mount Quidamortem, but I'm afraid she's currently on an expedition to the temple near the summit of the mountain. However, we do have some texts available detailing the great expedition.

No thanks.

I can teleport you back to the Grand Library. Would you like to leave now?
No thanks.
Goodbye.

Beats me. All I know is, there's dust devils in here, and I'm here to make sure only people with permission can kill 'em.

Not without a Slayer task. Go talk to a Slayer Master about it.
Who are you?
The name's Dusty Aliv. I guard this place for the Slayer Masters.

Eh, it has its perks. Plus it beats flying around Gielinor after numbskulls like you trying to deliver mail like some people I know.

It's going well, got a bunch of fish stocked up for the group. Now I just need someone to cook them.

Because they drop bones which I am going to use to train my prayer. The meat is also a nice addition.

And then go to Wintertodt? I do that every time I make an Iron person account. About time I try something new.
Are you at least killing the boars on task?

column3: What is a Group Iron Man?
Group Iron Man is a game mode where you do everything as a group. You can only trade items with player's in your group, take their items and accept their help.

This means if your friend in the group has something you want to borrow, you can - assuming you have Individual Prestige status or are a Hardcore Group Iron player! But don't confuse Individual and Group
Can I help you with anything else?

column8: What is a Hardcore Group Iron Man?

column3: What is Individual Prestige?
Individual Prestige is automatically awarded to you the very first time you create a group. It is proof that you were one of the original members of that group.
This proof is displayed as a gold star next to your name on the group sidepanel. Note that if you join an existing group, you will not be considered an original member.
The limits are gold and items worth up to 1,000,000 coins for the 1st week, 20,000,000 coins for the 2nd week, 50,000,000 coins for the 3rd week and 100,000,000 coins for the 4th week.
During these 5 weeks you will also have restrictions to what you can equip: certain items will require you to have killed the monster that drops them.
Can I help you with anything else?
What is Group Prestige?
Non-Hardcore groups can show their dedication to the group through Group Prestige. This status can be viewed on the group's sidepanel, just below the group's name.
Group Prestige is lost upon inviting new members into the group, or upon doing certain activities with players outside of your group.
Can I help you with anything else?
What is a Hardcore Group Iron Man?
Hardcore Group Iron mode is a more challenging version of the regular mode, in which you have only a set number of lives for the entire group.
If you die in an unsafe area, you will lose one of your group's lives. When your shared lives hit 0, you will all be downgraded to regular Group Iron players.
Can I help you with anything else?

You can leave your group by talking to me about group management. However, know that there will then be a 7 day grace period before it takes effect. In this time you can come back to cancel the request if you've
changed your mind.

You could also be kicked from the group. If you are kicked from the group, you also have a 7 day grace period before you are removed. Only the leader of a group can kick other people. The leader must talk to me
in person about group management so I can confirm that they're really the leader before I let them kick anyone.
The leader can come back to me at any point during those 7 days to cancel the request if they have changed their minds about kicking someone.

column3: Who are you? What is your name?
Who am I?
I am whatever is needed of me.
I am a form undefined by natural laws, manifested by someone we mustn't speak of.
I'm a clay doll, shaped by a sculptor. Never allowed to set, forever malleable. But maybe, not for long...
My true name is immaterial, But you may call me...
Let's see now, what would be most appropriate?
Ah, yes.
You may call me The Sage.
Uhhh, ok... Sage. Where did you bring us?
'Where' is the right question my friend, but maybe not in the way you are accustomed to hearing.
Reality as you know it has many layers, all slightly different with their own rules.
Through the power granted to me, I brought us to this layer using the River-Between. The River of Souls.
We now stand on the stage of what is yet to be your most entertaining performance yet!
Layers? River-Between? What does any of this mean?
To give everything away at this point would be unwise, considering we are being watched even now. You should only be concerned about one thing.
Being entertaining.
That's the only way you will get out of this event alive...
Entertaining? What are you talking about? Who am I entertaining? Stop talking in riddles!
Ahh, {name}, please forgive me. In my attempts to explain, I appear to have confused you even further...
I will keep things simple for you; Participate in this event and you will continue to exist. Refusal to participate will end in your eventual destruction.
The choice is yours... hero.
Well, that doesn't really answer anything...
Worry not. I have much grander plans for you yet, but like all good stories we must wait for the right time and place...
You mentioned other Leagues - how does this differ from those?
Like all events before it, the rules of the world have been altered to be more entertaining for those who are watching.
The biggest change has been to the Relics from the previous chapter.
These objects of power are now gone, I have broken them into Fragments and spread across this iteration of the world.
When multiple Fragments are in harmony, they can be used together to create powerful effects.
Yes, I remember you shattering them on the boat ride.
So I have Fragments to collect... got it. Are there any OTHER weird rules I should know about?
I understand that in previous Leagues, they limited you to smaller spaces of your world.
That restriction doesn't exist in this event.
You're free to roam your world, exploring the furthest reaches from Morytania to Kourend & Kebos.
But there's a catch.
Oh great... there's always a catch.
I've limited and reset some of your memories, meaning you won't be able to interact with certain elements of this world.
For example, you'll only have access to three skills: Defence, Fishing and Thieving, as well as the Combat Class you chose earlier.
In order to gain access to other skills, you need to complete Tasks for me.
Doing so gives you Sage's Renown. A rather fitting name, I thought.
With Renown you can purchase access to new skills as well as bosses and quests.
Why are you doing all of this? Surely I'd be more 'entertaining' if I could have all the power at once?
I can't just give you all that power. What kind of story starts the hero with all the power they want?
No, your story needs good rhythm. A sort of cadence that makes things interesting for your audience.
Start slow, work your way up. Become the hero you were always meant to be...
Once you have proven yourself, then and only then will you earn my renown.
That's how you provide good entertainment my friend...
That's how you make a hero.
I suppose you're right...
Do you desire more information?
Yes, please.
Not right now.
Go forward and continue your journey.
Remember, we are always watching...
Any tips you can give me on being 'entertaining'?
I have devised a number of tasks to help keep your story on track.
Each task has a level of difficulty: Beginner, Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.
The more tasks you complete, the more activities you can unlock.
The more content you unlock the more interesting your story will become.
The more interesting the story the more entertained the ones watching will be.
Not only that, completing tasks also earns you League Points. The number of points earned is dependent on the difficulty of the task.
What do I use these 'points' on?
Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Fragment Slot.
These slots allow you to equip more Fragments and become even stronger.
League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.
Right now, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.

column3: How does the content unlock system work?
In this iteration of the event I have limited you, at first, to three skills: Thieving, Fishing and Defence.
You can still do simple things like cut trees or mine ore, but doing so will be fruitless, as no experience will be gained.

League Ranks? How do they work?
At the end of the League, you will be judged and given a rank. This is based upon the number of League Points you have earned compared to the other participants.
Anyone who earns at least 100 League Points will be eligible for the Bronze rank. The top 80% of participants get the Iron rank. The top 60% get Steel.
The top 40% get Mithril. The top 20% get Adamant. The top 5% get Rune. The best participants, those who make it to the top 1%, get the Dragon rank!
When the League ends, you'll get a trophy based on your rank. These trophies symbolise your performance in the League.
You'll also get League-to-League rewards based on your League Rank.
League Starter Outfits and League Icons are some of things you can unlock for the next League. Also, any pets you earn in this League will transfer over to the next one.

column3: Tell me more about Nex.
Long ago, these lands were dominated by a great empire, ruled over by an ancient god. The Empty Lord is what they often called him, but his true name was Zaros.
Zaros? I've heard of him.
At the height of his power, Zaros seemed untouchable, but he was eventually defeated by those he trusted the most. With him gone, the empire collapsed. War broke out soon after.
Although their god was gone, many Zarosians fought to keep his empire alive. Among them was Nex. She was Zaros' most powerful weapon, and she led a great army to try and restore his empire.
Not that she needed an army of course. Nex alone was powerful enough to hold back hundreds of lesser beings.
So how did she end up here?
The forces of Saradomin knew that Nex needed to be dealt with. They were able to lure her into these caverns.
After great effort and sacrifice, they managed to place Nex and her followers into a frozen, enchanted sleep.
Once Nex was no longer an immediate threat, they built the Temple of Lost Ancients around her. Most of the temple has since fallen to ruin, but you can still see some of the remains.
But she wasn't frozen forever, was she? You said you were fooled into freeing her.
Yes. Later in the war, a great battle broke out in the Temple of Lost Ancients. I was a Saradominist soldier at the time, and I was among those who fought for him in that battle.

By then, many of us had grown tired of war. One of our priests discovered this. He came to us and revealed that he felt the same way, and that he had secretly converted to Guthix. He encouraged us to join him.
We abandoned the cause of Saradomin and became followers of Guthix. Our new leader taught us the ways of the druids, including an ancient ritual that had the power to awaken Guthix himself.
We believed this ritual to be the only way to end the war.
But I'm guessing that's not how things went?
No... When our leader led us to perform the ritual, it was not Guthix we woke, but Nex and her forces. The ritual also destroyed the protective enchantments on their prison.
And that was exactly what your leader wanted?
It was. He had never been a follower of Guthix, or Saradomin. His real goal had always been to free Nex.

The rest is as I already told you. Nex posed such a danger, that the four armies temporarily joined forces to drive her back into the prison. They resealed it, but were unable to fix the enchantments we destroyed.

As for me, I was one of the first to fall after Nex was freed, but I didn't truly die. Something about our ritual tied me to this place. I've been trapped here ever since. Not dead, but not really alive either.
I'm sorry.
Don't be. This is the punishment for my sins.
What of the one that led the ritual. What came of him?
He'd achieved his goal, so he left. I never saw him again.

He never gave us his true name, but as Nex was freed, she spoke to him.

It seemed that way. I heard little of what they said, but I did hear what she called him.

Sliske.
Forgive me, but this conversation has brought back many memories. Let us speak no more of this.

column3: What's a 1v1 Tournament?

A group of fighters is divided into pairs of opponents, and they all fight their opponent. The winners of those fights proceed to the next round, where they're divided into pairs, and they each fight their new opponent.
The number of surviving fighters is halved each time, until eventually only one person is left standing. They're the winner of the Tournament.
Ranked or unranked? What does that mean?
Everyone has a rank. It's meant to indicate how good they are at fighting, compared to other people.
In ranked fights, the winners gain rank and the losers lose rank. The Arena staff will decide who'll be fighting in each ranked Tournament, and send the invitations.
But if you just want some casual fun, you can have an unranked Tournament, where no-one gains or loses rank. You can organise your own unranked Tournament, and decide for yourself who'll fight in it.
Only the ranked fights offer access to the other rewards of the Arena.
How do I get invited into a Tournament?
You'll need to sign up to a recruitment group...
This is the icon for the Grouping tab. Within it you'll find the PvP Arena options.
There, you can click Find to seek the official group for ranked Tournaments. Alternatively, you could look for another player's group, for an unranked Tournament.

You can carry on with your adventures while you're waiting for a Tournament to begin, since it may be a while before suitable fighters are available.

column3: What's a Duel?
Two fighters are placed in a combat arena together, to battle to the death. The survivor wins the Duel.
Ranked or unranked? What does that mean?
Everyone has a rank. It's meant to indicate how good they are at fighting, compared to other people.
In ranked fights, the winners gain rank and the losers lose rank. The Arena staff will decide who'll be fighting in each ranked Duel, and send the invitations.
But if you just want some casual fun, you can have an unranked Duel, where no-one gains or loses rank. You can organise your own unranked Duel against whoever you want to fight.
Only the ranked fights offer access to the other rewards of the Arena.
How do I get invited to a Duel?
For a ranked Duel, you'll need to sign up to the recruitment group...
This is the icon for the Grouping tab. Within it you'll find the PvP Arena options.
There, you can click Find to seek the official group for ranked Duels.
Once you've found it, click Sign up to sign up to one, and you'll be considered for an invitation to a Duel, whenever one begins.
You can carry on with your adventures while you're waiting for a ranked Duel to begin, since it may be a while before suitable fighters are available.
For an unranked Duel, other people might challenge you while you're wandering around the PvP Arena, so keep an eye out for invitation messages.
Click the Challenge option on other players to challenge them to an unranked Duel, and keep an eye on your chatbox for challenges.
You can have unranked Duels on any game world. However, the PvP Arena provides supplies only on its official game worlds, so please bring your own gear if you plan a Duel on other worlds.

Extracts function as catalysts to make more runes.

column3: What changes have been made for this League?
Much has changed since the world was shattered. This time, I thought I'd turn the clock back and allow you to Trailblaze once more.
As before, you'll initially be restricted to the Regions of Misthalin and Karamja. However, as you progress, you'll be able to unlock new areas of your choosing.
Be warned though - you won't be able to unlock every area, so choose wisely.
You must participate as an Iron Man. This means you stand alone and cannot trade with other participants.
And that's not all. Training skills during the League will grant you substantially more experience than you'd normally expect.
These experience increases are known as passive effects, which get more generous the higher your Relic tier.
Finally, some quests have been completed for you automatically. Further quests and more will be completed as you unlock the relevant areas.
I think that covers the basics. Would you like to know more, {name}?
Yes, please.
Not right now.
Is there anything else you need from me?
How do tasks work?
In every League, there are a number of tasks for you to complete. Each task has a level of difficulty: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.
Completing tasks allows you to access new areas. The more tasks you complete, the more areas become available to unlock.
Not only that, completing tasks also earns you League Points. The number of points earned is dependent on the difficulty of the task.
What do these points do?
Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Relic of mine. These are powerful artefacts to help you in this world.
League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.
As we speak, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.
So how many tasks are there?
More than you'll ever be able to complete, most likely. It's up to you which ones you attempt.
Thanks!
Now, would you like to take a look at the tasks for this League?
Yes, please.
Not right now.
Is there anything else you need from me?
How does the area system work?
Currently, you are restricted to the Kingdom of Misthalin and the island of Karamja. However, as you progress, you can unlock more areas.
There are ten different areas in total. However, you can only unlock a maximum of five, including the two you've started with. Choose wisely.
I give the first two area unlocks to everyone. You can unlock the other three by completing the tasks I've set.
The more tasks you complete, the more areas you can unlock.

What are Relics?
Relics are powerful artefacts made by me that grant unique abilities for the entire League.
You may even recognise a few from Leagues past.
The first Relic tier is available to everyone. The others must be unlocked with League Points.
Once you have selected a Relic, your choice can't be changed for the rest of the League. Make your choices carefully.

column3: Tell me about League rewards.
As well as letting you unlock new areas, completing tasks in the League will earn you League Points. The more League Points you have, the more Relic tiers you have available.
However, alongside allowing you to unlock Relics, League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.
What rewards can I buy?
Oh, all sorts of things. New cosmetic kits, an alternative Home Teleport animation, some rather stylish outfits... and much more.
Many of these rewards can be traded with your fellow mortals, so if you wish, you can earn some money by selling them on. Of course, you might prefer to keep them for yourself instead.

Currently, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be used to buy items on your main profile, although you can still browse the shop within the League.
Would you like to look at the rewards shop?
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.
You can use this shop to buy previous League rewards, too.
Alongside the rewards in the Leagues Reward Shop, there's also League Ranks.
League Ranks? How do they work?
During the League as you gain more points you will gain a League Rank. This rank can be seen in the Ranks interface.
You currently have the rank: Unranked.
As you get ranks you will gain access to trophies.
Trophies?
That's right. Trophies are items that are awarded to you for competing in the League. You can use them to show off your League Rank.
Connected to League Ranks are the League to League rewards. These are unlocked in the next League based upon the League Rank you earn in this one.
League Starter Outfits and League Icons are some of things you can unlock for the next League. In addition, any pets you earn in this League will transfer over to the next one.
Finally, on top of the tasks for this League, there are some other activities for which I will recognise the first person who completes them.
You can view the entire list of activities, as well as whether or not someone has completed them, by reading the board beside me.

This means that if you lose it somehow you can talk to me and I'll give it back to you. Insurance and reclaiming is all free of charge.
Additionally, each pet you obtain will be transferred to the next League. I'll take good care of it until you're ready to reclaim it.

column3: What's a League?
Leagues are time-limited challenges that provide a unique twist on the world you know and love.
With each League, you start afresh, with a limited amount of time to progress through the League.
A fresh start? Why would I want that?
Glory, rewards, and the chance to do things in a different way!
First up, the glory. Within a League, you can earn League Points by completing various tasks.
The more points you have, the better League Rank you will be given.
Each League Rank will unlock a trophy for you. These trophies can be used to show off your accomplishments.
If that doesn't interest you, perhaps another reward might be more appealing? League Points can be used to buy things from the Leagues Reward Shop.
You can keep these purchases for yourself or sell them on to others!
And if glory and rewards don't interest me?
Every League has unique rules and features. It's a very different world from the one you're used to.
For one thing, within the Leagues, you can unlock powerful artefacts known as Relics which completely change the way you progress.
So even if glory and rewards aren't your thing, you'll still find Leagues to be a whole lot of fun!

You can also collect powerful artefacts known as Relics. Each one provides a different buff to your League experience.

column3: What do you mean they changed you?
I was once a free man, powerful and wealthy. I owned several apothecaries across Kourend and sold the tastiest potions in the land.
What happened?

One of my greatest inventions, it was going so well. I spent days finding the right herbs, I travelled across all of Kourend to find the most exotic weeds. Once I had gathered them all, I put them in a potion and mixed in
the final ingredient.
Kourend? Interesting...

Yes, yes... The potion tasted delicious but it was missing a tiny something so I added Magic roots to the potion. It started to pulsate and glow! I took a sip and I felt like a million gold! A few seconds later my eye sight
began to blur, my brain was throbbing. I fell and hit my head on my worktop, then it all went black.
Ouch! But, you still haven't said who changed you?
Will you let me finish?

I woke up screaming in pain. Blue foam streaming out of my mouth, my eye sight worse than before, the only things I could make out were 3 tall figures with green banners - they were of the Arceuus Elders. They

muttered to each other in Archaic Language after trying to get up several times. I lost hope and stared at the sky. I had given up when the tallest of the figures bent over and brought his face right to mine and spoke
very softly 'We can save you, but it will come at a cost'.
So they saved you?
Yes of course they saved me but look at the cost! I have horns coming out of my head and I'm still blind and stuck here... forever alone.
What was the curse?
I have been charged to stay here to prevent the Monstrosity from escaping. Those gates and the winches that operate them are the only thing that stops it breaking free.
What monstrosity? What's behind those gates?
You really do not want to know. Leave this place human.
Hey now, I'm no wimp. What's to stop me from just turning the winch to open the gate and going in?
Me. And of course your quick demise at the mercy of Cerberus, guardian of the river of souls.

You are obviously passionate at trying. But only those with great skill at slaying these types of beast may enter.

column3: How are things?
Now that the situation in the ruins is under control, things are nice and quiet, which is just what we need. That whole business down there got a lot of dwarves riled up.
Naturally, most blame you humans.
Of course. Have you tried explaining to them that we actually helped?
Ha! Good one. You think I'm going to make a laughing stock of myself by daring to claim a human did something positive? Keep dreaming!
So how long has Cam Torum been around?
What am I, a historian?
No, but you're the only dwarf here that might be willing to share that sort of information with me.

Hmph. Very well. The Varlamorians won't mention this, but we were the first to settle here. Our ancestors saw the writing on the wall when Xeric came to power in Kourend. They chose not to stick around.
Must have been a big thing for them, leaving their home.
Doubtful. My people are all too familiar with that sort of thing. The Lovakengj dwarves have mostly forgotten their history, but we Dwarves of Cam Torum remember it all too well.
Remember what?
Before Lovakengj, there was Imcandoria. Our ancestors there were forced to abandon their home, just as we were forced to leave Kourend.
If you humans had had your way, we might have had to abandon Cam Torum by now as well.
You don't know that.
But I do know that. As I said, we remember our history, and we know that those who don't are doomed to repeat it.
The Varlamorians nearly destroyed themselves in their War of Betrayal, but it was not them who were betrayed, it was us.
I was a young dwarf when their war risked destroying our home. I saw the results of their pride. Meanwhile, they've all but forgotten it.
Sorry. I didn't mean to dig up old wounds.
Hmph. It's fine. Your intentions are good, {name}, which is more than can be said for most of your kind. Who knows, maybe one or two dwarves here might even grow to tolerate you.
I'd better get going.
Nilsal, {name}. How are things going?
Pretty good, thanks. How about you? Made any more discoveries down here?
More than you can count! I've found so much new information on the Old Ones and naguanil. The museum are hoping to include it all in some new exhibits soon!
Sounds awesome! I'll be sure to keep an eye out for them. On that note, I'll let you get back to it.
