column3: Could you tell me more about the early history of Varlamore?
Certainly! When it comes to the existence of Varlamore, it is Xeric we have to thank. During his Age of Strife, many refugees fled Kourend over the previously unexplored Custodia Mountains.
There were three notable groups of these refugees. The first group, the Talkasti, settled in the Tlati Rainforest.
While they initially lived nomadic lives, they eventually started to establish more permanent settlements, with Tal Teklan being the first.
The next group were the Pericans. They first settled right here, building the town of Fortis, or Civitas illa Fortis as it eventually became.
Finally we have the dwarves. These were refugees from Lovakengj who established a home beneath Ralos' Rise, becoming known as the Dwarves of Cam Torum.
Was there any friction between these groups initially?
Oh yes, very much so. The dwarves, just as they do today, mostly kept to themselves. However, the Talkasti and Pericans came into regular conflict over various matters.
But that's not the case now, right? What brought them together?
As you may well have already guessed, it was religion. Long before leaving Kourend, the Talkasti had taken to secretly worshipping Ralos and Ranul.
After arriving here, they were able to openly practice their religion for the first time. Over time, the Pericans started to adopt this religion as well.
As the two groups came together, the population of the region started to rapidly expand. This eventually led to the construction of Tempestus, and with it, the founding of Varlamore.
So are there still distinctions between the Talkasti and the Pericans now?
Yes and no. Those terms are no longer used to describe people today. Since we united, we have all been Varlamorians. However, you'll still find many traces of our previous divide.
For example, here in Fortis, you'll find yourself surrounded by Perican architecture, whereas over in the Tlati Rainforest, the influence of the Talkasti remains clear.
Names are another good example. Indeed, look no further than our rulers. For most of our history, we were ruled by the Tullus dynasty, with Tullus very much being a name of Perican origin.
However, we are now ruled by the Arkan dynasty, whose name can be traced back to early Talkasti nomads.
I see. So where did the name Varlamore come from.
The name comes from the River Varla that separated Talkasti and Perican territory. What was once a symbol of our divide, became the symbol of our unification.

Could you tell me more about religion in Varlamore?
Of course! Whereas in other parts of the world you'll likely find followers of many gods, here in Varlamore, you'll only really find those dedicated to Ralos and Ranul.
Losanium is the official term for this religion, though it is not a term you'll find used very often.
How come?
Losanium encompasses the worship of both Ralos and Ranul, and while they do indeed go hand in hand, it is rare to find individuals equally dedicated to both.
Instead, most people focus their worship on one of the two, with Ralos being by far the more popular. Something that isn't too surprising given Ranul's association with death.
Now that said, you might actually find a higher than normal number of Ranul worshippers right here in the museum.
Something that is easily forgotten is that while Ranul is indeed a god of death, he is also a god of learning and knowledge.
If you wish to learn more, you may well want to seek out one of the teoki in the temple to the south. Though of course, they may well have somewhat biased takes on their religious practices.

Could you tell me more about Varlamore's recent history?
I can indeed! When it comes to recent events in the kingdom, the best place to start is with the War of Betrayal. It all started around 100 years ago when Imafore Tullus ascended to the throne.
He soon reorganised the kingdom into the Varlamorian Empire, a controversial choice to say the least, though it soon became clear that controversial choices were quite popular with Imafore.
While public opinion was always mixed, nothing he did resulted in outright conflict until his sudden and brutal murder of the Kourend Royal Family. War was quickly declared.
Until that day, Varlamore had successfully managed to avoid conflict since before the kingdom was officially established. To say the war was unpopular would be an understatement.
Imafore soon found himself facing as much resistance from within as he did from Kourend. The end result was predictable.
Imafore and his forces found themselves trapped between two armies at the Battle of the Proudspire. He was captured and executed, bringing an end to the Tullus dynasty.
This brings us to a fun little fact. After his death, Imafore was succeeded by King Mezpah Arkan. One of his first acts was to call for the beheading of every statue of Imafore in the kingdom.
The statues remain to this day. It's actually a crime to try and remove them. They exist as a reminder of our history, and a warning to any who would try to follow in Imafore's footsteps.

So how has the kingdom changed since Imafore died?
The War of Betrayal was very much seen as a wake- up call. While Varlamore had once flourished under the traditions of the Tullus dynasty, by the end, it's fair to say we were stagnating.
King Mezpah set to work on transforming the kingdom. His ambitions were high, to the point that much of what he desired never came to pass in his lifetime.
One of his most notable goals was to see Varlamore open more widely to the outer world. A goal which thanks to his great-granddaughter, has now finally been achieved!

Indeed. We would often send our students on trips to the east prior to the opening of the borders. The amount of paperwork needed was astounding! Now we can just hop on a ship any time we like!

I have a selection of both rare and common furs from all across the kingdom. Also, if you happen to have any furs you've brought from the east, I'd be pretty keen to buy some.
So, want to trade?
No thanks.
Tetamo! If you change your mind, you know where to find me.
Gems! Get your gems here!
Let's trade.
I'm good, thanks.
Then move along please!
A little bit of spice makes everything taste nice! Come and get it here!
Let's trade.
I'll pass.
Your loss.
You've tried the rest, but how about the best? Our baked goods won't be beaten!
Let's see what you have.
I'm good.
Hmph!
Nilsal, iknami. Welcome to my farm. Are you in need of some farming supplies?
Yes please.
No thank you.
As you wish.
Hi there. Looking for something new to wear? You've come to the right place if so.
Let's see what you have.
I'm good, thank you.
No worries.
Welcome to Cobado's Groceries. Feeling hungry?

column6: Why do you have an orange on your head?

column3: Let's see what you have.

Why don't you have an orange on your head?
Er... Because it's not an item of clothing?
Not for you perhaps, but it is for me.
Right...
So anyway, looking to buy some food.
I'm good.
Well come back when you're hungry.
Nilsal. Here to do some crafting? I've got some supplies that might help you if so.
What do you have?
Have a look.
Just passing through, thanks.
Well come back if you change your mind.
Welcome to The Flaming Arrow. What can I get for you?
Let's see what you have.
Nothing for me, thanks.
As you wish.
Welcome to Atlazora's Rest. If you're in need of a drink, then you're in the right place.
Show me what you have.
I'm good, thanks.
Fair enough.
Nilsal. Do you wish me to exchange banknotes for you? I charge only 10 coins for each banknote.
Yes please.
Then hand me the banknotes you wish me to exchange.
Who are you?
I am Virilis. I can exchange banknotes of bones for real items. Do you want any banknotes converted?
What can I do here?
I'm glad you've asked! Next to me is an old altar of Ralos, upon which you can ask for bones and wines to be blessed.
You should beware though, Ralos won't hear your prayers if you aren't experienced enough. I wouldn't want you to get caught in the cold just waiting for nothing to happen.
Anyway, once you've had Ralos' blessing, you can break the bones down into shards. Then, along with your blessed wine, you can take them to the libation bowl and sacrifice them in Ralos' honour!
Libation bowl?
Yes! You'll find it inside the Teomat, near the library.
I see. And what happens if I drink the blessed wine?
The last person to try that ended up in the libation bowl. I do not recommend it.
Anyway, do you want any banknotes converted?
No thanks.
Nilsal, {name}.
Hello, Zuma. How are things?
A lot less stressful up here. I think I might leave the adventuring to people like you from now on.
Still, at least it gave me a lot to talk about. Those Moons of Peril are concerning, but exciting! I just wish we knew more about their potential links to Ranul.
So you still think there is a link?
Oh yes. It may not have been the one I originally thought, but there must be something! They're called Moons after all!
The all-powerful Ranul wouldn't have just let some random creatures take on a name like that!
Hmm... It's an interesting thought.
Indeed. And on that note, I have some research to do! Until next time.
Nilsal.
Hello there. What brings you here?
I am the teoki responsible for the Colosseum. I am in charge of all that happens here.
Hang on... The Colosseum is run by a priest?
Well much of the day-to-day running is handled by the Colosseum Master, but yes, I am the one in overall charge of this place.
So why is that?
This is more than just a place of spectacle. You stand in one of the holiest sites in all of Varlamore. Each drop of blood spilt here is a glorious offering to Ralos.
It is these offerings that sustain him. Without them, he will not have the strength to light our way.
Interesting... Thanks for the information.
Forgive me, my child, but I have little time to talk. There is always plenty of Ranul's work to be done here in the Colosseum.
Hello, there!
Hello! The name's Kit. Sir Kit Breaker.
Sir Kit? That's a nice name!
Thank you! I chose it myself!
... Thinking about it, I chose mine as well. I'm {name}, by the way.
Very nice to meet you!
What do you do around here?
I'm helping Gilbert with a project of his, on behalf of the White knights. It will take us a while but I can let you know when we're closer to completion!
Sounds good!
Hello there. I have a message for you.
You've been given a message.
Hello there. What do you do here?
Ah, I'm just keeping an eye on things and making sure nothing untoward happens.
That's reassuring.
One day I hope it will be.
Hello there. What can I do for you?
What do you do here?
I mainly take in washing and make sure it's good and clean for my customers. Times are tough though. Not everyone can afford such a service and it's affecting my takings.
Do you find that very fulfilling?
Well it can be a bit monotonous and the pay isn't good, but I set myself some goals and deliver my washing clean. My customers rarely complain, so I guess I must be doing something right.
The broav greedily eats the mushroom.
Hello there, {name}.
Hey, Idria. How are things here?
Busy. No doubt you're already aware that Lucien has set his sights on Guthix's Archive. We've had to expend a lot of resources to ensure it is defended.
However, while defending the Archive is essential, we must also remain focused on Lucien himself.
He has the Stone of Jas and the Staff of Armadyl now. That should give him everything he needs to follow in Zamorak's footsteps, but for whatever reason, he's chosen not to act yet.
Is there anything I can do?
Only what you're already doing. Help with the defence of the Archive where you can. We'll be sure to let you know the moment Lucien himself makes his next move.
Sounds like a plan. Thanks, Idria.
Hello there. What are you doing here?
Oh, nothing much. I'd just heard Draynor was a nice place to visit.
Fair enough.
Hello there.
Good day to you. I've prepared this patch for you to plant the enriched snapdragon in.
Okay, thanks.
Hello there. What are you doing here?
That's not really any of your business, is it?
Fair enough.
Can I help you?

column3: What are you doing out here?
This here is the Warrior's Guild, a place where the strong may train. I'm the one who decides if you are allowed in or not.
Am I qualified to enter?
You may not enter the Warrior's Guild as you are right now.
What? But I'm a warrior!
While you may consider yourself a warrior, I do not.
Go on, let me in, you know you want to. I could... make it worth your while...
Go away and train small one. I do not take bribes.
Why not?
The Warrior's Guild has a code of honour, a code that I respect. Move along.
I'm here to talk about Combat Achievements.

column4: Could you explain what they are?

column3: Could you explain what they are?
Combat Achievements are a set of tasks for all adventurers to try and accomplish. They range from simple missions to kill various creatures, to challenges that will push you to your limits.
The purpose of these tasks is for you to grow and improve, experience all that Gielinor has to offer, and become stronger in the process.
Is this something that sounds interesting to you?

column4: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.

column3: Yes, tell me about Combat Achievements.
Combat Achievements are broken down into six tiers: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, Master and Grandmaster.
As you complete tasks, you'll earn points. Tasks in higher tiers give more points than easier tasks. Your rank depends on how many points you've earned.
Whenever new tasks are added to the list, there are more points available to earn, so the threshold needed for each rank will increase. Keep completing tasks to maintain your rank!
This is the icon for the summary panel. Within it there is a section for Combat Achievements.
Clicking on the section will open the Combat Achievements interface, where you can browse tasks, bosses and rewards.
Some tasks will require numerous criteria to be completed, so make sure you read them carefully.
I'd recommend you go kill some monsters. Come back to me when you've completed a tier or two. I'll reward you for your efforts.
Thanks a lot, I'll get going.
Not at the moment, no.
I have to go.
No, I'm alright thanks.
Hello, I'm Laidee. Welcome to the Warriors' Guild.

That I am. Ghommal and I used to adventure together before we joined the Guild. It felt only right that I take over from him. It is... strange not having him around.
I'm sorry for your loss. He was a great warrior.
And an even greater friend.

column3: Tell me about the strength training area.

Ahh the mighty warrior Sloane guards the strength training area. This intriguing little area consists of two shotput lanes for different weights of shot. It's fairly simple, the Referee or Sloane can explain more. You
may find yourself panting for breath though.
Oh? Why?
Well you see my dear boy, the games there really do sap your energy quite a bit. You can find it just up the stairs behind the bank.
Tell me about the attack training area.
Ahhh, dummies.
I'm no dummy, I just want to know what is there!

Oh no my dear man, I did not mean you at all! The training area has mechanical dummies which pop up out of holes in the floor. The noble dwarf Gamfred invented the mechanism and Ajjat can explain more about what
to do there.
Oh, ok, I'll have to try it out!
You can find it just down the corridor and on your right.
Tell me about the defence training area.
To polish your defensive skills to the very highest level we've employed a most inventive dwarf and a catapult.
You're going to throw dwarves at me?
Oh my no! I think Gamfred would object to that most strongly.
He's an inventor you see and has built a marvellous contraption that can throw all sorts of things at you including magic missiles...
Mmmm?
....spiked iron balls.....
Err....
....spinning slashing blades....
Ummm...
... and even anvils.
ANVILS!?
No need to be afraid, it's all under very controlled conditions! You can find it just up the stairs behind the bank.
Tell me about the combat training area.
Ahh yes, our resident magician from foreign lands created a most amazing gadget which can turn your own armour against you! It's really quite intriguing.
That sounds dangerous. What if I'm wearing it at the time?

So far that's not happened. You need to speak to Shanomi about the specifics of the process, but as I understand it, putting a suit of armour in one of these devices will make it come to life some how. The better
the armour, the harder it is to 'kill'.
Fighting my own armour, that sounds... weird. I could be killed by it...
Indeed we have had a few fatalities from warriors over stretching themselves and not knowing their limits. Start small and work up is my motto! That and go see Lidio for some food if you need it.
Ok, thanks for the warning.
Tell me about tokens.

Ahh, yes, our token system is designed to allow you an appropriate amount of time with my discovery in the very top floor of the guild. I won't spoil the surprise as to what that is. Go up and see for yourself. Now, the
amount of tokens you collect from the various activities around the guild will dictate how long Kamfreena will allow you in the enclosure on the very top floor. More tokens equals more time.
So what's up there?
If I told you it would spoil the surprise!
Ok ok... so how do I earn and claim these tokens?

You can earn them simply by using the training exercises around the guild, the staff will then enter this into a ledger as you play. You can claim them by simply asking any of the staff at the training areas, or
myself.
Sounds easy enough.

Not really... no.
Why I could best any person alive in a rapier duel!
Try me then!

My dear sir, I couldn't possibly duel you, I might hurt you and then what would happen to my reputation! Besides, I have this wonderful guild to run. Why don't you take a look at the various activities we
have. You might even collect enough tokens to be allowed in to kill the strange beasts from the east!
Bye!
Farewell brave warrior, I do hope you enjoy my guild.

column10: May I claim my tokens please?

column3: Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?
Sure. You can buy a skillcape when you reach level 99 in a skill. Apart from boosting your statistics in that skill, they can also be used to perform some pretty amazing emotes!
The Cape of Strength also provides you with unlimited teleports to our guild. Is there anything else you would like to know?
What can I do here?
Ahh, the shot put is a great test of strength and can be quite rewarding. Mind you do it properly though, you might want to dust your hands with some powdery substance first. It'll give better grip.
I'll remember that. What should I use?
I personally prefer ground ashes, it makes a nice fine powder and gives some really good grip.
Ok, what else?
Basically you'll need to go in there, make sure you've got nothing cluttering up your hands, pick up a shot and throw it.... depending upon your technique, you can get quite long throws.
What was your best?
Ahh that would be telling...
That's a big axe!
Yes indeed it is. Have to be mighty strong to wield it too.
But you don't look that strong!
Maybe, maybe not, but I still had to beat a Barbarian to get it. Mind you, usually they don't part with them. This was an unusual circumstance.
Oh?
I bet him he couldn't catch a squirrel whilst still holding his axe but that I could... and that if I won I'd get his axe.
What happened?

He went running after the squirrel... nearly caught it too... it shot up a tree and he tried to climb up it, only got a bit tangled up with his axe cause he couldn't hang on to it at the same time... he fell out of the tree and it
was my turn....

I simply went and chopped the tree down with this big old axe, still holding it. The squirrel was so petrified it simply jumped straight out of the tree onto me, I won the axe and let the poor creature go!
I sense a moral in there somewhere.
Aye indeed. Brawn isn't all you need to wield a big axe, brains are required too!
May I claim my tokens please?
I'm afraid you have not earned any tokens yet. Try some of the activities around the guild to earn some.
Ok, I'll go see what I can find.
Bye!
Ah, hello there, warrior.

Well...there's a story to that. You see, I should have an axe but-
Sloane's axe?
My axe. He won it because of a squirrel.
A squirrel?
He bet me that I couldn't catch the squirrel while still holding my axe, but that he could... Thing is, he tricked me! When it was his turn, he just chopped the tree down!
I see. That doesn't explain why you have a tree branch though.
A barbarian warrior is bound to his axe. I cannot take up another, so I use part of the tree that Sloane cut down as my weapon... It also reminds me of him.
He was a great warrior.
Yes, and a good friend, Still, he would want us to be happy that he is now with his warrior brethren. Can I help you with anything else?

Ok, I'll go see what I can find.
Bye!

I'm one of the elite Slayer Masters.
What's a slayer?
Oh dear, what do they teach you in school?
Well... er...

I suppose I'll have to educate you then. A slayer is someone who is trained to fight specific creatures. They know these creatures' every weakness and strength. As you can guess it makes killing them a lot easier.
Never heard of you...
That's because my foe never lives to tell of me. We slayers are a dangerous bunch.
Wow, can you teach me?
Hmmm well I'm not so sure...
Pleeeaasssse!
Oh okay then, you twisted my arm. You'll have to train against specific groups of creatures.
Okay, what's first?
Sounds useless to me.
Suit yourself.

Boots alone do not make an Araxyte.

I want the adventure to end.
Hello!
Leave me be. I am not here to make friends.
Fair enough.
Hello there!
Hello! You're not from around here, are you? It's exciting to see that even people from outside of Varlamore are looking to join the Emissaries!
Well after I heard about all the good work they were doing, I could hardly say no! What about you? What made you want to join them?
Well it's our duty of course! The Church of Ralos has become lost, but the Emissaries know the truth. Ximoua will not come to be unless we make it so!
So you're quite eager to see the end of the world then?
End? Ximoua is no end! It is the beginning! We will all come together as one and bring about a new world! I can't wait!
Well I'm glad to see you're so excited. Good luck with the tests.
And you!
Hello!
I'm not sure I should be here. Maybe all this was a bad idea.
What makes you say that?
I want to help... I want to believe... I really do! It's just all so intimidating...
I'm sure it will be fine.
I hope so.
Hi there!
Greetings, iknami. It's good to see so many who are willing to contribute to the Final Dawn. The word of the Augur has changed everything. The time to act is now.
Augur?
You have not heard? She is the one who now leads the Emissaries. She has taken this once helpless collective and turned them into the ones who will guide us all to Mokhaiotl.
How do you know all this? You're not even a member yet.
I was once. In my time of need, I turned to the Emissaries, but they were even more helpless than I was.
Now though, she has changed everything. Now it is my duty to rejoin their ranks so that we may bring about the Final Dawn.
I see. Thanks for the information.
The people of this world do not have the strength to do what must be done. Ximoua will only come to be if we make it so.
We seed the hidden truths of this world! Ranul rewards all of us who are willing to find them!
Greetings, friend. Our time grows ever near. Ralos and Ranul will unite us all as one, and we will create a new world.
You! Time for some questions.

column4: Why did you join the Emissaries?
column8: Tell me about the Final Dawn.

column3: Why did you join the Emissaries?
To do my duty, of course. Ralos and Ranul wish us to bring about the end of this world. Only then will we see the birth of a new one.
Who do you worship?
I worship both Ralos and Ranul equally, for in reality they are one. They have been separated for now, but soon they will rejoin once more.
Tell me about the Final Dawn.
The Final Dawn is our destiny. Ralos and Ranul will unite us all and end this world, but in doing so, we will all play a part in forming a new one.
You! Time for some questions.

column4: Why did you join the Emissaries?
column8: Tell me about the Final Dawn.

column3: Why did you join the Emissaries?
I always knew people were wrong about me. I knew I would serve a higher purpose. I never cared what it was. I only cared that in doing so, I would be serving the will of Ralos.
Who do you worship?
I have served Ralos my whole life. I am his humble servant. It was he who guided me here so that I may serve his will.
Tell me about the Final Dawn.
The Final Dawn is an end, but also a beginning. It is when Ralos will use his holy fire to destroy this world so that he and Ranul can build a new one.
You! Time for some questions.

column4: Why did you join the Emissaries?
column8: Tell me about the Final Dawn.

column3: Why did you join the Emissaries?
To be honest, I wasn't too sure about joining at first. My friend convinced me though. Here we're part of something bigger than ourselves.
Who do you worship?
I've never been one for proper worship, but I believe in the teachings of Ralos and Ranul. I hope those teachings guide me through whatever is to come.
Tell me about the Final Dawn.
They say the Final Dawn is inevitable. It's the end that we can't escape from. It's a scary thought, but the Twilight Emissaries have embraced it, so I have as well.
You! Time for some questions.

column4: Why did you join the Emissaries?
column8: Tell me about the Final Dawn.

column3: Why did you join the Emissaries?
I wished to see my god in mortal form and serve his will. In return for my service, the Emissaries promised me they could grant that wish.
Who do you worship?
I am a humble servant of Ranul. It has always been my hope to stand before him and be judged as worthy.
Tell me about the Final Dawn.
The Final Dawn is the will of Ranul. He will show us all that death is nothing to be feared as he and Ralos guide us into forming a new world.
Who are you?
My name is Brew'ma. I'm here to assist adventurers like you with potion making.
If you hand me a herb from the Bruma tree and one of the unfinished potions from the crate, I can combine the two if you lack the... talent to do so yourself.
Thanks!
Welcome back, friend. Can I interest you in a kebab?
Yes please.
No thanks.
Well, you know where to find me when you change your mind.
Need something?
Had any more minotaur problems recently?
Not since you killed that one. The beastmaster reckons there was a problem with it imprinting. Happens from time to time.
Imprinting?
Yup. They're meant to imprint on the beastmaster as soon as they're born, but this one seemingly didn't. As I say, it sometimes happens.
I see. Well, hopefully I don't find myself coming up against any more rogue minotaurs.
Nilsal, iknami. I can't stop to talk I'm afraid. We're having trouble with one of the alpacas again
Don't mind me, but if you're looking for something to do, this man here needs a hand.
Well, I never imagined you'd be quite the actor!
I have to admit, I rather surprised myself there.
I don't suppose you'd like to be acting here in the future? To be honest, I'd prefer you to that odd fellow that brought you to my door.
It's a kind offer, but I'm afraid it was a one-time job.
A shame to be sure.
Anyway, do feel free to wander around the villa whenever you fancy. I don't recommend drinking from the wine fountain though.
After all that, are you sure I can't convince you to join the union?
Actually, I was wondering if...
Kuani! I'll need to run and grab my forms, but if you wait there just a moment...
I was going to ask if you had any spare equipment...
Spare equipment?
I may have a need to mask my identity again in the future... or perhaps carry a tray around.
You're certain you don't want to join the union as well?
I'm sure.
I see. In that case, which equipment would you like?
The ram mask.
The head butler hands you a ram mask.
Thanks!
The wolf mask.
The head butler hands you a wolf mask.

Well it's the Moonrise Brewery and Winery who own this place. It's only as nice as it is because of their continued investments.

The lab under our feet allows us to fund our research by producing useful products for the kingdom.
So you do things differently to the druids of the mainland?
In a way, but we very much respect Herblore as a profession and recognise that whatever your druids do definitely works. Our goal is to advance the study of Herblore, not replace it.
Anyway, I'm a little busy at the moment, but I'm sure some of the other lab assistants would love to tell you more!
What do you do around here?
When I'm not working in the lab, I'm normally somewhere around here researching or administrating our orders. There's an awful lot of paperwork to get through!
Can I buy some potions?
We're not really a shop, so our products are not available to buy directly. Everything we make gets shipped wholesale around the kingdom.
You look like the adventuring type anyway. I can't imagine our products would be of much use to you.

You alchemists sure wear a lot of safety gear.

Nothing. I'll be going now.

The location ended up being quite appealing for some as well. It makes for a nice change of scenery for those that appreciate that sort of thing.

Nothing much of note. The land here was owned by the Moonrise Brewery and Winery, but they found it wasn't much good for growing grapes.
So they were happy to give it up?
Very happy. They saw an opportunity for a new business relationship. In return for giving us the land, we now give them favourable rates on what we mine here.

column3: How do I brew ales?
Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick. Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
How do I brew cider?
First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush. Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
What do I do once my ale has matured?
Well, once you've got a full vat of the good stuff, just turn the valve and your barrel will fill up with eight pints of whatever your chosen tipple is. Mind it's an empty barrel, though.
Do you have any spare ale yeast?

Well, as a matter of fact I do, although I wouldn't describe it as spare. This ale yeast I've got is the best money can buy, but if you've got a pot I'll fill it for you for 25GP - very cheap as it happens.

Okay then, why not.
Okay then, why not.
Yes, you fool?
Excuse me?
You looked like you wanted to speak to me, you halfwit. You dullard.
That's enough.
My contract stipulates that I must follow you, you insufferable ignoramus. My contract does not stipulate that I must be polite, you ignorant buffoon.
What have I ever done to you?
How about parading me around like a trophy, you idiot clown? How about stuffing me in your rotten backpack, you inclement cretin? How about-
Hello there.
Hello. Here for a drink? You've picked the right place if so.
Nilsal, iknami. Thank you for saving my life in that cave.
It's my pleasure.
After what happened, I've decided to make some changes in my life. First up is less work. Next is more drinking!
More drinking?
Well, not too much more. I wouldn't want to become known for it. I just plan to relax and enjoy myself a bit more.
Well, I can't blame you for that. All the best.
And to you, iknami.
You found those people who went missing! Did you see them? Did you see the night people?
Sort of. I wouldn't call them people though.
But they're real! They're actually real! No one believed me, but I knew they were real!
Well, congratulations I guess...
Please leave. We're not in the mood for visitors.
I hope they come home soon...
Good day, traveller.
Hello there. I was wondering if you could tell me anything about the missing people.
Not really. We put a lot of effort into finding them, but nothing came of it.
Where do you think they went?
Well, some say they got lost in the mountains. Others say they decided to go and live somewhere like Fortis instead of here. I'm not too sure myself. It is a large number of people who've vanished...
But you stopped looking?
It was taking up a lot of resources. We don't have a huge number of guards here, so I need to use my people wisely.
If we get a new lead, I'm happy to send them out again, but right now it's like looking for a needle in a haystack.
I see. Thanks for the information.
Hello there, traveller.
What's going on here? Where is everyone?
Most are in the city. As for the rest, hopefully somewhere nicer than this place.
In the city?
Yes. When we heard they were going to lock Menaphos down and shut the gates, most people here decided they'd be better off behind the walls than outside them.
But you stayed?
We didn't get much warning. People had to rush to gather whatever they could. Some things had to be left behind, along with some people...
That's horrible!
It could have been worse. Had we been in Sophanem, we'd have had no warning at all. I just hope it won't be long before things are back to normal.
I hope so too.
Thank you, traveller. Stay safe out there. These are troubling times.
Hello there!
Tetamo! This is a total disaster!

Imps!
Imps?
Yes! I don't know where they came from, but my basement is filled with them! At best, they're stealing all my things, but at worst, they're just destroying them!

Thank you for the offer, but I don't think so.
Fair enough.

Gus barks happily.

Like I said, this is Nemus Retreat. Back during the War of Betrayal, this was a military camp for Imafore's army, run by none other than General Nemus himself!
General Nemus is something of a hero in these parts. Towards the end of the war, the forces of Kourend had mostly taken the Auburn Valley.
As a result, Imafore ordered General Nemus to burn the entire valley to the ground to stop the Kourend advance. Many would have died on both sides, but Nemus refused the order.
Imafore had him executed as a traitor, but in doing so he lost the support of all of Nemus' troops.
Sounds like a bit of a shortsighted decision.
Indeed. Imafore presumably hoped to make an example of Nemus, but instead his decision was one of the final mistakes that ultimately led to his defeat a few months later.

Anyway, ever since the war ended, this place has remained here as something of a monument to Nemus. Of course, rather than a military camp, it now acts as a nice stop off for travellers such as yourself.
And on that note, can I get you a drink?
I'm good, thanks.

I would suggest you speak to my counterpart instead. Those of us dedicated to Ranul do not specialise in that sort of thing.
What's the giant tree stump all about?
This stump is all that remains of the Great Auburn Redwood. It was, and in many ways still is, one of the key holy sites of Varlamore.
What happened to it?
The tree was destroyed during the War of Betrayal many years ago. It was here in the Auburn Valley that the fighting was at its most fierce.
Both sides resorted to tactics that most would consider to be beyond horrifying. The tree was sadly a casualty of such tactics.
Which side was responsible?
That has never been clear. Ranul teaches us to find and preserve the truth, but in war, the truth is sadly left behind.
So the battles that took place here... Is that why all these animal spirits are here now?
Yes. They are the spirits of the animals that died here during the War of Betrayal. They did not pass on to Mictl, for they have unfinished business in these lands.
What business?
That is beyond our understanding. We believe they are here to guide the ents that live in the valley so that they may one day regrow the Great Auburn Redwood.
The ents can do that?
Much of the valley was destroyed during the war. Most of what you see around you was regrown by the ents.
That's incredible!
Indeed it is, my child. That is why it is our duty to ensure the ents are protected. The events of the war cannot be repeated.
I'd better get going.
Then go in peace, my child.
Nilsal, my child. I hope you are enjoying your time in the valley.

I'd better be off.
May the sun light your way, my child.
Hello there! You look like a hunter. What are you on the hunt for?
Nilsal! I'm actually out here writing reports on the animals of the forest.
I see. Made any interesting observations so far?
Well, it would appear that a number of them are somewhat incorporeal...
Yes, I'd actually made that observation myself. I imagine being incorporeal means they're somewhat harder to hunt?
You could say that.
What about the ents? Anything interesting to note on them?
Yes, in between avoiding being stepped on by them, I've been trying to see how they interact with the other animals... specifically the corporeal ones.
Truth be told though, they don't really seem to be affected by them. They just keep on their merry way.
Interesting... Well, if you need any help with any of this stuff, do let me know.
Thank you for the offer, but I think I'm good for the moment.
Fair enough.
Nilsal. Are you here to watch the ents with me?
I wasn't explicitly here for that, though I'm sure I could stop for a moment.
You really should! They're such fascinating creatures. I could stay here for hours!
Have you ever wondered what sort of a tree leaves a stump this large?
What if it was an ancient ent that grew too big? Can you imagine that walking around?
Imagine...
Got anything shiny I can swipe?
If I did, do you think I'd tell you so that you could then swipe it?
You make a fair point.
Nilsal, traveller. What brings you out here?
Just exploring. What about you?
You'll find me here quite often. I like to come and tend to this grave.
Whose is it?
I don't know. I don't understand the markings on it. They are not of this land. All I know is that it is the grave of someone from Kourend.
They'll have been a soldier of some sorts, fighting here in the war. I'm guessing they were quite important. Very few people would have been afforded a burial in those times.
If you don't know who they are, why tend the grave?
It was my father's generation who fought in the war, but they're all gone now. My generation will soon follow. In time, this grave will go as well. Eventually, they'll be no trace left of the war.
I guess that's why I tend the grave. The future is inevitable, but for now, I'd like to try and hold onto the past for a bit longer.
I see. In that case, I'm sorry to have disturbed you. I'll leave you to it.
Thank you, traveller.
Hello there.
Can I help you?
Just wondering what brings you out here?
This is the only land border into the Kingdom of Varlamore. We're here to make sure no one enters without permission.
I see. Would I be able to enter?

No. The Queen is currently making arrangements to allow outsiders like yourself to enter Varlamore without needing to obtain permission first. However, until then, you must remain on this side of the border.
Fair enough.

That I would like to know myself. Tecuani left to attend to business elsewhere in the kingdom, but is yet to return.

Timoiva, and may the sun light your way.

No worries. You know where to find me when you need me!
Where can you take me?
Currently, my service runs from here to Tal Teklan and then on to the Gloomthorn Trail on the edge of the Auburn Valley. I make the most of the river currents to move rapidly from point to point.
The best part is, I make enough money doing deliveries, so if you just want to travel, it's entirely free of charge!

Fair enough, iknami.
So there I was, minding my own business on the boat, when I feel us slow to a halt.
This man walks over to me and says that it's my stop, absurd though that is.
So they all sort of... toss me onto this island with a meagre amount of survival objects.
I think they were laughing whilst they did it.
Either way, there I was. Alone. On this island.
I'd paid quite handsomely for my passage too!
A tour to the rainforest, and then dinner in Tal Teklan.
This crew were all so very willing to get me where I wanted to go.
Very helpful as they collected my belongings. Eager, even.
It felt exclusive. I was the only passenger they took aboard.
I do see now that I was perhaps foolish.
Drawn in by their charms, throwing money around.
I just really wanted that dinner in Tal Teklan, you know?
Now I'm going to die alone on an island, bereft of my worldly possessions.
Perhaps the bards of Temptestus will write of my sorrow, should they hear my tale.
Tell people of my struggles!
I can't believe she's done this.
Who's done this?
Fabia! She asked me to meet her, and I quote, 'by the special tree'. You may notice that she isn't here! I've been waiting for hours!
Do you think she might just be delayed?
I know her too well. She wouldn't be delayed coming to see me.
Could you be at the wrong special tree?
No! This is the one, singular, special tree!
Humour me for just a moment. What if, amongst this entire rainforest, there's a second very similar tree?
And Fabia would find herself at the wrong tree in this scenario?
Or maybe it's you who is at the wrong one?
No, absolutely not! I know where to meet Fabia and I wouldn't miss any opportunity to do so!
This was the tree where we first met. It was a lovely day! A botanical tour of the rainforest, but the only thing I found myself looking at was her...
Well, I'm sure the two of you will find each other soon. However, I do suspect that might happen sooner if you considered looking by some other trees...
Hmm... I'll think about it, but for now, I'll wait here a while longer.
I can't belive Xilo hasn't shown up.
Were you expecting to meet someone here?
My... friend, Xilo. I told her to meet me by the magic trees of the rainforest. We don't often have a chance to meet without a crowd of people around.
Why? Is she not particularly local to you?
Unfortunately not. I'm from Aldarin, but she lives in Tal Teklan. It usually takes a special event being hosted for us both to be in the same place.
So you never really get any privacy?
Privacy? Are you insinuating something?
Not at all. Sorry if it seemed like I was.
It's okay... Sorry... I just miss her.
Do you think she's just running a little late?
It's possible.
Could she maybe have considered another tree magical?
I suppose she may be where we first met... but this is where we shared our first... you know...
Well, I'll keep my fingers crossed for you. I'm sure you'll be able to find one another soon!
Thank you, iknami.
Oh, I do declare! Another perambulating soul traipses through this verdant forest!
Er... Hello there.
Salutations, my good compatriot! Pray, what curious happenstance is it that brings yourself out to my sylvan domicile?
Your... domicile?
The rainforest! A most resplendent deviation from the cacophonous tyranny of urban existence.
It's certainly more colourful, that's for sure.
Indeed! Out here, one may emancipate themselves amidst blissful tranquility.
I see... So how does such a... magniloquent individual... come to be out here?
Well, it commenced when I was merely a youth, and has proceeded uninterrupted ever since.
You came out here as a child?
I was most fortuitously deposited within this locale by my progenitors, along with this extravagant bundle of novels. Behold this one!
The odd individual shows you a book.
Er... That's a thesaurus.
What an exquisitely scandalous read it was. Now, you seem like someone who appreciates linguistic variety! Would you care to partake in a spot of intellectual cultivation with me?
I'm not sure if that's quite...
I possess a cornucopia of literary marvels. This one by Di. C. Tionary is captivating.
The odd individual shows you another book.
A dictionary?
No! Di. C. Tionary. She's one of the foremost novelists of our time. Such an unparalleled way with words. I'd love to have an audience with her some day.
Tell me, have you met any of the literary greats?
I've not had an opportunity to.
A tragedy, to be unequivocally certain.
Yes... Anyway, I think I need to get going now...
Very well! I shan't exasperate you with excessive and superfluous conversation. Besides, my tomes beckon. Farewell.
See you around.

Surely business is quite slow then? There aren't many humans around here.
Not on the island itself, but we do sometimes allow human vessels to dock here for trade. However, truth be told, I don't need to do much trading with them these days.

Indeed it is, young one. There has always been a tortugan fletcher in charge of the Trial. Before me it was Elder Manna, who taught me all that I know. Before him it was Elder Sarr.
Eventually, I will be succeeded as well. There are many tortugan adults out there who studied under me as juveniles. One day, one of them will take on my role.

Every adult will one day return to the Conch. With their adventuring days at an end, they will settle here as an elder.

Whenever that happens, it is a chance for us current elders to consider if the time has come to take a step back. Soon, it will be time for me to hand over my duties, but until then, my work continues.

column3: Who are you?

The name's Kellan. Used to be a daft-hand at trawlin' back in m'day before the muscles began achin' and the bones started creakin'. These days are better spent helpin you young'uns get yer foot in the trade.
How do I deep sea trawl?
Well, it all starts with you buildin' a good ol' trawlin' net on yer boat. Rope will do, but linen, hemp and cotton are preferred. The better ye' net, the deeper ye'll be able t' lower it.
After ye' got a net, ye' need t' find a shoal out at sea. In mos' cases, different shoals 'ave different fish, so make sure yer lookin' for the one ye' want.
Once ye' find a shoal, it'll probably be on t' move. They travel o'er pretty large distances, but ye'll find 'em stoppin' from time t' time. Once they stop, that be when it's time t' start catchin'.
So that's when I need to lower my net?
Aye, exactly. However, it's important for ye' to know that different shoals be at different depths, and plen'y of shoals will be swimmin' up and down as well.
Yer gonna need t' lower the net to the same depth as the shoal, but remember, if the shoal is too deep and yer net ain't up to scratch, yer gonna be all outta luck.
Okay, so I get a good trawling net, find a shoal, wait for it to stop, and then lower the net to the same depth as the shoal. What else?
If yer wantin' to catch plenty o' fish from a shoal, then yer gonna 'ave to bait it. Best time t' do that is just after it's stopped. For the bait, ye'll be needing lots o' fish offcuts.
Ye' can get some offcuts by cuttin' up any kind o' fish, but fancier fish like shark an' such will give ye' higher quality ones.
And I'm guessing the fish in some types of shoals are only going to be interested in higher quality offcuts?
Aye, ye' learn fast, laddie.
So these offcuts... Do I just throw them into the water?
Well, sort of, but ye'll need t' proper equipment to do it. Specifically, ye'll want to build a chum station on yer boat. They're what ye' use to spread t' offcuts.
Finally, don't forget that shoals travel o'er big distances. If ye' don't feel the shoals in ye' bones, ye' can build a fathom stone on yer boat. They can help ye' track down a shoals whereabouts.
I see. This is all very different to normal fishing.

Well, if trawlin's not yer style, laddie, ye' can always cast a rod o'er the side o' the boat and pray they be nibblin', but it's less effective than nets are an' it burns through yer' supply o' bait.
Where can I deep sea trawl?
Ye' can do it wherever ye' can find a shoal. They're all across the ocean and yer got different ones fer different fish. I can tell ye' some good places t' find specific ones.
First up, krill an' haddock are the best shoals for gettin' started. There be a great spot for krill just west o' here in the Great Sound.
Ye' can also find both krill an' haddock down in t' Unquiet Ocean, around places like Red Rock, the Great Conch and t' like.
Next ye' got yellowfin an' halibut. There be plen'y o' yellowfin in the Shrouded Ocean, such as near Deepfin Point. Halibut are extra easy! Ye' can find 'em right outside this here port!
Bluefin are more scattered. Ye' can't really pin 'em down, but I'd try farther south near the waters full of tangled kelp.
And then ye' got marlin. They can only be found in the' frigid Northern Ocean, but only the best o' boats can survive up there.
If yer put off by some o' the risks, ye' can try to get lucky. Shoals like t' migrate, an' sometimes them rarer fish mix and mingle with t' other shoals.
What kind of fish can I catch while trawling?
Well, there's giant krill, haddock, yellowfin, halibut, bluefin, and if yer up fer a challenge, the elusive marlin.
These ain't yer normal brand o' fish either. Some say that these are the tastiest fish ye' can get. Some even provide unique effects when ye' eat 'em!
Do you have any other advice for me?
I'm sure ol' Kellan can think o' some stuff t' help ye' on yer trawlin' adventures, laddie.

First, ye'll want t' get yer hands on some sturdy fish crates t' hold more fish. Skilled craftsmen can make empty crates out o' camphor logs then ye' pack em full o' ice. Them slayer masters often have ice fer sale.
Second, trawlin' is always better with a good crew by yer side to delegate up the workload. If ye' go it alone, ye'll be trying to man both t' net and chum station at t' same time!
Third, remember that them rarer shoals don't just stay at one depth. Yer gonna find 'em swimmin' up and down. Ye' gotta pay attention and make sure yer net matches their depth.
Finally, don't be forgettin' to bait the shoal when it stops! It'll attract more fish to yer' boat.

column3: Could you tell me about Barnacle Barnaby?
He was a cruel and vicious pirate. Orchestrator of the Driftwood Massacre and unleasher of the Plague of Black Mists. He believed himself untouchable, but his arrogance was his undoing.
Despite the warnings of many, Barnacle Barnaby attempted to plunder the Skullhorde, but his only reward was a deadly curse. It destroyed the Crimson Kraken, condemning all on board to a watery grave.

And risk the wrath of Barnaby's ghost? No. I thought it better the map be locked away, so that neither it nor the curse could harm anyone else, but those young fools put an end to that.

column3: Can you tell me more about port tasks?
Sure thing, mate. You'll find that a lot of ports will have a notice board where folks have gone and stuck up some ads for jobs they want sorting.
Might be they want some cargo lugging about, or maybe they're after someone to pop out and do a bit of killing for them.
And is there anything I should keep in mind while doing these tasks?
Well, after you've gone and accepted a task or two, you'll want to keep your captain's log handy. It's good for keeping tabs on what jobs you're currently grafting away at.

Also, if you're doing a bit of courier work, you might find it handy to get a couple of crewmates on board. They can help you shift the goods about so you're not knackering yourself by carrying one crate at a time.

Well, mate, sea charting is all about heading out and improving your own knowledge of the sea itself. Your captain's log has all sorts of cracking tips on how to do so.
If you want to know more, your best shout's going to be heading down into the cave on the island for a chinwag with Charles. He's the local expert on this sort of stuff.

Can you tell me more about shipwreck salvaging?
Well, as the name suggests, mate, it's all about salvaging old shipwrecks from the sea. Keeps the place nice and tidy, and allows you to snag some swag from those that don't need it anymore.
To get started, you're going to want to head over to the shipyard and sort yourself out with a proper nice salvaging hook. The flashier the hook, the quicker you'll be able to salvage.

Once you've got your hook all nicely set up, it's time to head out and find a shipwreck. You've got plenty of different types to pick from. Once you spot a good one, just use the hook to get stuck in.
You'll want to keep salvaging until you're feeling chuffed with your haul. Then you just need to use a salvaging station to sort through it all. Any half-decent port's going to have one.

If you're a bit of a cheeky sod yourself, you might want to get involved in one of their trials. All of them are about speeding around and clocking the best time possible.

Anyway, if you fancy it, the nearest one is just south of here in the Storm Tempor. Just don't go being a lemon and jumping in without a boat that's up to the task. Last thing you want is to go and sink!

column3: What changes have been made for this League?
The great and terrible demon Yama has bound this League to his will.
Once again, regions contain monstrous Echo Bosses that can be defeated to earn unique and powerful rewards.
Yama, in his wisdom, has granted you the ability to augment your powers through Demonic Pacts. You may earn Demonic Pact points by completing Demonic Pact tasks.
Unlike before, you'll initially be restricted to the single Region of Varlamore. However, as you progress, you'll be able to unlock new areas of your choosing.
Be warned though - you won't be able to unlock every area, so choose wisely.
Additionally, Misthalin will not be available at all this League, and once you reach the first task threshold Karamja will be unlocked for free.
You must participate as an Ironman. This means you stand alone and cannot trade with other participants.
And that's not all. Training skills during the League will grant you substantially more experience than you'd normally expect.
These experience increases are known as passive effects, which get more generous the higher your Relic tier.
Finally, some quests have been completed for you automatically. Further quests and more will be completed as you unlock the relevant areas.
I think that covers the basics. Would you like to know more, {name}?
Not right now.
Is there anything else you need from me?
Can you tell me about Demonic Pacts?
Demonic Pacts are new powers granted by Yama that modify and improve your combat abilities for the entire League.
Why would Yama want to give me more power?
It wouldn't be very entertaining to see you go up against Echo Bosses with your mortal prowess now would it?
At least, not for very long. Death comes easily to your kind.
I see.
You can earn Demonic Pact points by completing specific combat tasks.
These points can be spent to unlock abilities and progress through the pacts in a manner that suits your preference for combat.
There are many choices available, but you will not be able to select them all. Plan ahead and choose wisely.
Now, would you like to take a look at the Demonic Pacts available to you?

Very well. Is there anything else you need from me?
How do tasks work?
In every League, there are a number of tasks for you to complete. Each task has a level of difficulty: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.
Completing tasks allows you to access new areas. The more tasks you complete, the more areas become available to unlock.
Not only that, completing tasks also earns you League Points. The number of points earned is dependent on the difficulty of the task.
What do these points do?
Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Relic. These artefacts have been reshaped by Yama and his cohort to grant new powers.
League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop.
As we speak, you are playing on your Leagues profile. The Leagues Reward Shop can only be opened on your main profile.
You can access your main profile by switching to any normal Old School RuneScape world. The world switcher in the logout menu can be used to switch worlds.
So how many tasks are there?
More than you'll ever be able to complete, most likely. It's up to you which ones you attempt.
Thanks!

How does the area system work?
Currently, you are restricted to the Kingdom of Varlamore. However, as you progress, you can unlock more areas.
Once you have proven yourself dedicated to the League, Yama will also grant you free access to Karamja.
There are eleven different areas in total. However, you can only unlock a maximum of five, including the two you are gifted. Choose wisely.
The first two area unlocks are given to everyone. You can unlock the other three by completing the tasks you have been set.
The more tasks you complete, the more areas you can unlock.

Relics are powerful artefacts made by me that grant unique abilities for the entire League.
You may even recognise a few from Leagues past.
There are 23 separate Relics, split across 8 different tiers. You can only have one Relic from each tier, however.
The first Relic tier is available to everyone. The others must be unlocked with League Points.
League Points are earned by completing tasks.
Once you have selected a Relic, your choice can't be changed for the rest of the League. Make your choices carefully.

You are far from many things in this place. Watch your tongue.
I'm going to speak to the Sage now since you're intent on being rude.
I don't care what you do as long as you do not interfere. Proceed.
I yearn for the Sage to defy master Yama, I shall feast on their broken body!
HAHAHAHAHA! What sweet meats there are to be torn from them!
Oh the energies I will devour...
Woah there, clearly you didn't have anything for breakfast today.
I am much more ferocious when I am hungry.
Hey, me too!
Don't make me laugh. You are puny, barely a morsel.
I disagree.
Hello.
Greetings.
So, what do you do around here?
I distribute buckets.
That's handy.
Indeed, Father Sugadinti's foresight is unparalleled.
Thank you.
Greetings.

column4: Could you tell me more about this place?

column3: Could you tell me more about this place?
It's a venator breeding ground. Father Sugadinti wishes for their numbers to be restored.
Interesting... So I can't kill any?
Not necessarily. The weak must be culled so the best specimens can thrive. As such, with a Slayer Master's permission, I will allow you to slay them.

Alternatively, are you aware of stymphikes? They prey on venator pups. Bring some feathers as proof of their deaths, either to myself or one of my fellow disciples, and we will allow you to kill some venators in return.
I may take you up on the offer some time.
I'd better be off.
Hello there, {name}. It's good to see you.

column4: I could use a new weapon.
column6: How are you feeling about being back here?

column3: I could use a new weapon.
Of course.
How are you feeling about being back here?
It is still strange. I no longer recognise any part of these lands.
Do you think they can ever go back to how you remembered them?
No. Sugadinti suggested that we rename Morytania back to Hallowvale, but I declined. Hallowvale will never exist again. It is nothing more than a memory now.
However, that doesn't mean we can't still create something new here. Morytania does not need to be the dark land it currently is. With time, a lot is still possible.
I'm glad Sugadinti has you to support him. Do you think you'll ever properly rule alongside him?
My days of leading ended long ago. However, I will always be here to help where needed.
That's good to hear.
How is Safalaan doing?
As well as can be expected. You saw for yourself the horrifying effects the vampyrification process had on him.
Vanescula said it was because of his icyene blood?

Indeed. Drakan called them wyrds. Far more powerful than a normal vampyre, but far more prone to uncontrollable hunger as well. He showed me one once. A little gloat about what he could do to my people.
But you've been able to keep that hunger in check?
As best as we can. He must feed. That is not something that can be avoided, but I have been making him potions to help him stay in control.
With time, I hope I can refine things further. We may even find a way for him to utilise the shapeshifting abilities possessed by other vampyres.
Well, if there's anything I can do to help with that, just let me know.
Thank you, {name}, but I think I have all that I need. It's just time and patience now. That said, while I do not need anything myself, I'm sure Safalaan would be keen to see you.

No doubt you've seen that Sugadinti has opened a new portal to Vampyrium. Safalaan has been spending a lot of his time there, helping the aranei with their work. I think he prefers to be away from this place.
Understandable. I'll make sure to check in and see how he's getting on.
I'd best get going.
Take care out there.
Welcome back, my child.

column6: I see you've opened a new portal to Vampyrium.

column3: How are things in Morytania?
Very good, my child. My disciples are providing a steady supply of their blood for the vampyres. As promised, the tithing of humans has been completely outlawed.
And the vampyres are all happy with that?
Most are understanding of the fact that regardless of anything else, the days of tithing humans were running short. However, it is true that some found human blood to be more... appetising.
I assume that won't be a problem?
You need not fear, my child. Any that attempt to take blood from a human will be dealt with harshly.

That said, my understanding is that some humans did willingly provide their blood to the Drakans. It is of course possible that could be explored again in future, albeit with very different arrangements.
However, I very much understand that will likely be a... difficult proposal for most to swallow.
Yes, I can't see many being up for that sort of thing. Speaking of which, how are the humans of Morytania doing?
The fact that they are not being tithed is on its own a significant improvement to their quality of life. However, their homes are still ruins and these lands are still dangerous.
We are offering our help in building them new homes, but it will take many years, and most are still naturally distrusting of our kind.
I'm guessing a lot will be more interested in starting new lives across the Salve.

You are correct, my child. However, while we have established somewhat of an... understanding with your human kingdoms to the west, it is their preference that we try to limit how many humans relocate over there.

They are not equipped to deal with a large number of refugees, and it is also our hope that many humans will realise they still have a place here. We will need their help restoring these lands to glory.
That's not going to be an easy undertaking.
It will most certainly take many of your human lifetimes, but I have no doubt we will make it so.
I see you've opened a new portal to Vampyrium.
Yes... While my disciples are currently providing blood for the vampyres here, I do not consider that a suitable long-term solution. Haemalchemy, I believe, will be the true answer.

With us having outlawed the practice of vampyrification, we have started using the labs to explore the creation of artificial blood instead. Curiously, we've already had some luck with daeyalt of all things.
It seems that the very substance that is the key to making vampyres can also potentially contribute to feeding them. While it makes sense in many ways, it was also rather... unexpected.
Interesting... And how does Vampyrium play into this?

Vampyrium is home to all manner of flora and fauna that cannot be found here. With the threat of Drakan dealt with, my disciples can freely travel to and from there, collecting samples to use in our experiments.

You are more than welcome to use the portal yourself, my child. Blood donations from Efaritay and my disciples keep it well powered, and it may be that you'll find Vampyrium to offer something of interest to you.
I'd best be off.
Until next time, my child.
Well, well, well. Back for more slaying?
Good day, friend. I hope that you are well.
Can I help you, outsider?
What are you selling?
Tell me about this shop.
This is the headquarters of Supplies's Supplies, a global chain of world class equipment providing outposts that effectively synergise with local corporate needs.
I'm sorry?
Excuse me, I wasn't done.
My apologies, please continue.
This business has been stimulating local economies for over one generation, and represents a core pillar of every community in which it operates.
We have locations at every major settlement on Wyrmscraig and a diverse portfolio of other business interests in the area.
Other business interests?
Supplies's Supplies has recently opened its own production facility for high tensile strength fastening cords.
I bought a yak and I'm using its hair to weave rope.
What are you selling?
I'd best be off.
No thanks.
Ah, what'm'ah gonna do with these damn goats...
Is there anything I can do to help?
Hrm... ye are an outsider... but ye do have a look about ye. Tell me, d'y'ave experience herdin' goats?
Uh... no?
Ah, a damn shame. If ye get some experience under yer belt, come back, but these goats aren't for the weak handed.
You need to have completed the Sheep Herder quest to hunt goats.
You finish crafting the golem from this angle.
{name}! Good t' see you!
Hi Cormac. How's the island?
We're learnin' to live a bit differently now that the Angel's gone... It feels a little odd, but we be makin' the best of it.
For example, thanks t' some notes that Keenan left behind, we've worked out how to make golems out o' sunstone. They do nay do much right now, but we reckon we can eventually make use of 'em.
Interesting...
Aye. Feel free to give it a go yoursen if you fancy.
Oh, by the way, one o' the others managed to find this sunstone crystal. Come back when you have space for it, and you can have it.
The woman seems despondent.
The smith remains focused on his work, casting an eye to make sure you aren't stealing anything.
Need something?
What are you selling?
Sorry, reckon I won't be doing business with you. Not 'til Cormac trusts you, at least.
Oh okay...
No thanks.
Catriona refuses to look at you.
Baldwin raises his eyebrows at you, but otherwise ignores you.
Hey, who are you, and what are you doing here?!
Oh, I just found this place while exploring the seas.
Hmm... We don't like outsiders here...
So am I not allowed to be here?
Well... I can't stop you, I suppose. I don't have the authority to do so... or the ability to, I guess. But make no mistake, I'll be keeping a close eye on you.
Angus turns his back on you when you attempt to speak to him.
Rian watches you cautiously, refusing to engage.
Slurp...
Greetings, adventurer. How can I be of service?
I'm not sure. What type of services do you provide?
I have a client in need of... specimens. I'll happily take any grown dogs off your hands.
What does your client use them for?
Hey there, I can take you somewhere safe if you'd like?
Arf arf!
The Chihuahua heads to the dog shelter.
Hey there, I can take you somewhere safe if you'd like?
Arf arf!
The Border Collie heads to the dog shelter.
Hey there, I can take you somewhere safe if you'd like?

The Corgi heads to the dog shelter.
